Klldarkness said:
See, I'm glad you point that out Bing, cause now I get to flex a lesser useful part of my college education.

Cause you're right! I was referring to the national level.

But, you're also wrong!

Prior to the 2023 reform, the prefectural specific laws you mention are referred to as the "prefectural youth protection laws". They did not include statutory rape level offense protection for youths, and were designed more as public-morality protections for minors rather than as full sexual-assault laws. Depending on which prefecture, most of them were less about consent, and more about inducing(Generally by paying, but did include other forms of coercion), sexual relations with someone under the age of 16-18. They also, of course, included laws about sexually explicit videos and pictures.

In most prefectures, if you were found in a sexual relationship with someone over the age of 13, but under the age of the local prefectural youth protection laws limit...the worst punishment was a fine of up to 3 million yen. In fact, most of the fines were less than 1 million yen. We're talking about less than $7k, at most $20k.

The most egregious cases(Imagine 13 year old and a 40+ year old), MIGHT see jail time, but even then it would have been 1 year or less.

The 2023 reformation raised the national level to 16, inline with a majority of the prefectural youth protection laws, but it also brought along with it all the actual consequences, such as statutory rape guidelines. Post 2023, Japan finally has real protections in place for those 13-17, and breaking them are tried at the federal level, which means real jail time and not pity fines.

Having said all of that I think Kumon-mi is outside of Tokyo, and Tokyo set the prefectural youth protection laws as 18, so Akira is liable to receive many fines for his various crimes of a sexual nature. He will also maybe lose his teaching license...It's also really sad that I need to say "maybe" cause it actually is a maybe. Japan wasn't exactly good about these things prior to 2023.

What im kind of asking/saying is do you people think its okay too feel so like i guess lack of a better word bad while engaging in things like this? Ofc it is made this way on purpose but i am sort of struggling with my feelings with this and wonder if people also feel off or weird when engaging with media? Also apologies if this makes no sense or isnt right to post here
Click to expand...
That's an understandable concern, I would imagine quite a lot of people might feel that way.

Overall I would say it's fine - even a good thing - to read something that challenges your sensibilities and gives you something to think about. One of the core themes in the game is a specific cycle of sexual abuse (which becomes much more apparent in chapter 4) and that in itself is an interesting thing to learn about in this kind of way. One of the interesting things for me with LiL and other VN's/games like this is that they can tackle things like this in a more upfront and provocative way with more nuance than you tend to see in mainstream media where subject matter like this is usually just put forward very two dimensionally, it all ends up just being samey and boring and not having anything actually interesting or insightful to add.

As long as you don't come away feeling like what you've read has been trying to encourage the behaviour or something I don't think there's a problem, personally, and I certainly don't feel that way after playing LiL.

jclark1337 said:
Idk imo this is one of the most mature and nuanced explorations of this kind of subject matter out there. It doesn't excuse or justify it, but really discusses the possible root causes and subsequent ramifications. The world needs a bit more actually contending with these kinds of dark realities head on in order to at least attempt at understanding and mitigating them, rather than pretending they don't exist and averting ones eyes from anything and everything controversial. Too many close-minded people nowadays.

I think he just doesn't care and has come to terms with the fact that if someone thinks his writing is weird or problematic then there is no point worrying about what they think anyways, because they will likely never think outside of the narrow box their mind works within
Click to expand...

It's not necessarily a bad thing to enjoy experience depressing and/or problematic stories. It helps us relate to our world around us in a more positive light because of the contrast ("well my life isn't THIS bad/fucked up at least.") Also can help people come to terms with their own trauma in a similar way.

A lot of ancient Greek and even Shakespearean tragedies were meant to teach us lessons on how to avoid human failures, and I kinda view media like this as a form of modern evolution of that idea but with more nuance. The "Lessons in Love" aren't lessons in how to find (possibly immoral) love like most porn game titles would suggest, but actually lessons in how twisted and consequential different interpretations of it can be.

Klldarkness said:
See, I'm glad you point that out Bing, cause now I get to flex a lesser useful part of my college education.

Cause you're right! I was referring to the national level.

But, you're also wrong!

Prior to the 2023 reform, the prefectural specific laws you mention are referred to as the "prefectural youth protection laws". They did not include statutory rape level offense protection for youths, and were designed more as public-morality protections for minors rather than as full sexual-assault laws. Depending on which prefecture, most of them were less about consent, and more about inducing(Generally by paying, but did include other forms of coercion), sexual relations with someone under the age of 16-18. They also, of course, included laws about sexually explicit videos and pictures.

In most prefectures, if you were found in a sexual relationship with someone over the age of 13, but under the age of the local prefectural youth protection laws limit...the worst punishment was a fine of up to 3 million yen. In fact, most of the fines were less than 1 million yen. We're talking about less than $7k, at most $20k.

The most egregious cases(Imagine 13 year old and a 40+ year old), MIGHT see jail time, but even then it would have been 1 year or less.

The 2023 reformation raised the national level to 16, inline with a majority of the prefectural youth protection laws, but it also brought along with it all the actual consequences, such as statutory rape guidelines. Post 2023, Japan finally has real protections in place for those 13-17, and breaking them are tried at the federal level, which means real jail time and not pity fines.

Having said all of that I think Kumon-mi is outside of Tokyo, and Tokyo set the prefectural youth protection laws as 18, so Akira is liable to receive many fines for his various crimes of a sexual nature. He will also maybe lose his teaching license...It's also really sad that I need to say "maybe" cause it actually is a maybe. Japan wasn't exactly good about these things prior to 2023.

If you want to get the Sensei Quest grind over as soon as possible on your own save, without doing anything weird with your save, do this:

Step 1:

Inside your game folder, find the senseiquest.rpy file

>



Step 2:

Inside senseiquest.rpy;

type CTRL+B, this opens the search bar.
type coins.mp3 in the search bar, this will lead you to the pink slime kill reward settings,
right below Play sound "coins.mp3" you will see the $ pcur += 10, this is basically what gives you money after killing a monster.



Step 3:

Get rich

All you need to do is change
$ pcur += 10
to
$ pcur += 1000000
and save the file
Now open the game, and kill one pink slime to get 1 million currency.
Once you've bought every item, save your file, open senseiquest.rpy again and change this value back to 10, make sure to leave no trace.

Congratulations, you saved 50 hours of your life.

Considering how surprisingly coherent this incoherent story is, I'd actually imagine it won't take nearly that long.

I'm not a glazer by any means, but I like to give credit where credit is due. Sel is a fantastic story teller, but what surprises me the most is how well he's managed to bring events together. Foreshadowing, and call backs, little points of reference to tiny events that happened years ago IRL.

That's not a skill you can learn to this level, it has to happen naturally by having a good memory of your own creation.

Back when I was a surprisingly famous fanfiction author, I was often praised for the same thing...but the truth of the matter is I was carried, not by my memory, but by that at the time I could read 900+ words per minute. I was able to read my entire collected works(300k words), in between every new chapter. It's easy to foreshadow and reference when you're reading your entire story twice a month.

Sel can't do that. Not with millions of words, there simply isn't enough time.

But, back to my main point:

The purity routes. Each one will require Sel to edit the entire story to allow for the possibility of each one. Any event that references sex with someone that isn't the focus of that purity route has to allow for that purity route. We're talking edits over the hundreds of hours, the millions of words.

It's unfathomably complicated.

To that end...the only way Sel could even consider the timeline he offered...is if he's already planning them as he goes. Making notes of events that need editing and additions, maybe even doing prep work inside the game to allow it, but not yet putting in the full effort.

Someone with Sels ability to keep this level of story coherent is likely the only kind of person that I think COULD undertake that level of addition at the end of a game.

Anything else is unreasonable, and likely impossible.

small edit:

I think maybe CharlotteWiltshire26 could also do it. They seem to have the exact right level of autism the task would require.

Ok, I’m at like, Chapter 3. I get what they’re trying to do with the protagonist. I just think the execution is horrible.

Of course, there’s several themes: he mirrors the player, reflects cycles of trauma, meaning of redemption, etc. But goddamn, he’s annoying, he doesn’t stop talking, and he never really changes.

Normally this isn’t a problem because this phase doesn’t last very long. But there’s so much bloat and rambling in this game that it feels like there has been zero progression with this protagonist for like, over a hundred hours of reading. Which is not good when you’re trying to make him an actual character.

Which is a shame because the girls, even if they feel a bit samey in terms of writing (man the metaphors just don’t stop), at least all have distinct messages and are moving through their various arcs. But there’s this increasingly apparent trade-off of like, “man, do I need to sit through another 10 hours of this protag say and do some stupid shit just to see Yumi try to put her family back together” or something.

I do like the worldbuilding though. But again, there's that trade-off that exists that's kinda annoying.

1) Cucking his brother implies he winning overall and I would definitely not say that. Like if an abusive father is fucking both his son and daughter and those two start fooling around to find some comfort in their shitty life, I wouldn't say the son is cucking the father. Noriko was the exception for several years, having hers on since her introduction despite only earning lust since last year. The wizards are not safe. I was going to say I'd be surprised if Io ever has an enabled lust stat, but she actually showed a decent amount of spine this cycle and can easily see how she could springboard from that into finding something to enjoy about sex, even if it's not the sex itself.

3) Main Girls = his class. No more, no less.

4) HOPE = Callous GOD during summer, WIRES = Calm God of winter, Pareidolia = Concerned god who became God during spring. (The Adjectives seem to be a intentionally unimportant plot point now)
HOPE is Nozomu, WIRES is the god who tends to alter reality with hallucinations. Pareidolia tends to be Black and white faces.

HOPE is Nozomu, WIRES is the god who tends to alter reality with hallucinations. Pareidolia tends to be Black and white faces.

posts.content_html_raw:
After being fundamentally fired as a creative collaborator in the previous Fan Fest here some fundamental issues with this year's FF:
First and foremost the biggest issue of FF2 is Sel blew his load way to early. Within the first week Sel ran through majority of the polls for the entirety of the FF. There are 4 1/2 or 5 weeks in March, Sel should've ran at least one or two polls a week. And the biggest mistake he made was doing the draft for Dorm Wars the very first week of the FF. It should've been during the last week FF, which would've been right before 0.58's development, which in turn would've generated more hype for the event. Other than the polls for the gravure set and the mini series there wasn't much to interact with because it was all gone within the first week.

Point #2: FF2 shouldn't have existed in the first place. The next FF should've been at the end of the game or year 10 of the game (if it doesn't end by then). The reason why FF1 was such a big success was because it was new and it celebrated a major mile stone, which was 5 years of LiL. Going into the next year, trying to recapture that same success without same merits of FF1 and 90% of the content being recycled is a task in itself. And in place of new ideas we got more filler(which I'm not really complaining about because Bunny Girl Yuki is something I never thought I needed). While I get Sel is doing something for the fans (trying to make more money). Something that would be more beneficial to the fans is a good update (or a good Dorm Wars update)! If need be Sel could've taken the month of and pumped out a quality update. Majority of the updates coming off breaks are good; an update that is very good is always going to resonate more with the fans than the FF. Or if that's not possible try something new. Nothing we got this year is fundamentally new with exception of Summer Vacation and the Amy extension. With a world as expansive and zany it's not hard to come out with fresh new ideas for the FF.

TLDR: Not enough fresh content, should've been used to celebrate major milestones.

Fanfest is dumb. Now that I've shared my nuanced opinion, let's get to the theorycrafting.

Theory: Pareidolia isn't in Sensei's head anymore because Ami sacrificed herself to get rid of him.
I think there is fairly good evidence (though not conclusive) that Ami offered herself as a sacrifice in a belief that it would protect Sensei from unspecified God(s). The Pareidolia part doesn't come from direct evidence, but rather by looking at timing along with the hints that Pareidolia/USER3 is involved in what's currently happening to Ami. I wrote about that in my last Ami post, here:
aramaug said:
A new update is nearly upon us, and you know what that means: it's time for me to hastily throw together a post about the last one before everyone has moved on. Let's talk about the main heroine true protagonist of Lessons in Love, Ami Arakawa.
Click to expand...
I still don't have a complete theory for what's going on with Ami, this post is just about tying together some of the evidence. I've been pretty thorough in posting everything I have noticed, not knowing what bits will be most relevant. So I apologize in advance if this post feels a bit scattershot.
After the Nakayarakawayama beach trip, Ami yells at Sensei about two things:
1. She does things for Sensei that he doesn't know about.
2. She refuses to let Sensei be driven mad by the gods, the way that her mom was.

Two lines later:

N.B.: She says "I will not lose you" instead of "I don't want to lose you." She's trying to prevent it.
I believe that these are connected, that what Sensei is unaware of is that Ami has been protecting him from God(s) (most likely USER3/Pareidolia). Early in Chapter 4, Ami told us how she would do it: by sacrificing herself and allowing the gods to "consume" her in his place.
Over the course of Chapter 4, Ami has hinted at her relationship with God(s), which has changed over time in tandem with her worsening mental state. In chronological order:
Chapter 4 starts with Sensei mentally broken after Maya's death. Ami recognizes that this leaves him vulnerable and warns him about letting gods in.

It's only a couple of events later that she floats the hypothetical of her sacrifice. If necessary, she'll act to prevent the gods driving Sensei mad.

In contrast, she seemingly has a positive view of "God" after Sensei comes out his coma. God told her that they're meant to be together, and she takes him at his word.

The contrast between these two is interesting. I'm thinking Ami realizes that she's being manipulated, but is so desperate that she chooses to believe it anyway. Or maybe she's already made a bargain with God at this point, and being with Sensei is supposed to be her reward.
Ami believed that Maya's "death" would change everything, that Sensei would stay inside with her forever. Instead, after he comes out of his catatonia, he goes right back to ignoring Ami in favor of being a manwhore. Ami has a breakdown and blames his behavior on God.

"Della" begins with a narrator, who I assume is Narrator Ami, telling a very strange story about "worms" inside of us which grow when we talk to God.

Ami rants about how Sensei doesn't act the way she wants him to, and comes to the conclusion that he's doing this because of his own worm - talking to God has made him like this. To get him back to "normal", she has to get rid of his worm.

Along with her rant, Ami mixes in lines from "The Gift of the Magi", because she identifies with a girl who sells a part of herself for the benefit of the man she loves. She is "selling" part of herself to God.

And because of that, she's now being eaten by a worm of her own. A worm that makes her act like a bad girl, when we all know that Ami is the best niece ever. Ami is the only girl I will ever need!
After "Della" it's Ami's turn to retreat to her room to recover from a traumatic experience/mental health episode. But while she does superficially get better, Narrator Ami suggests that her mind is continuing to deteriorate. Her worm is making her worse.

She leaves the house for the first time to go on the camping trip, where she has heart-to-heart with Sensei and shares a new outlook on God.

I'm speculating here, but I think Ami is able to catch a second wind because she reaches a state of acceptance. It's like a terminal patient who has a brief recovery shortly before things take a permanent turn for the worse. Ami had been fighting God's influence, especially after she blamed her worm for hurting Sensei in Della. But by the time of the camping trip, she now regards her worm as necessary suffering, a test from God that she must persevere through.

That brings us to seventh reset. Pareidolia abruptly leaves Sensei's head, claiming that he's sacrificed himself, though he conveniently can't remember why.

How likely is it that Pareidolia, an amoral hedonist, would make a selfless sacrifice? Maybe he's trying to claim credit for Ami's sacrifice?

Regardless, Pareidolia has "parting gifts" before he leaves, and it's implied that one of them is sending Nodoka to the world where Sensei and Makoto end up during the reset (side note: I assume this is Ami's wish world). This disturbs the "happy ending" of that world's Ami and activates her murder hobo mode.

I've speculated that Evil Ami came to Sensei's world from this happy ending. (I was wrong about a payoff coming in the eighth reset, but otherwise I still stand by that post.) By sending Nodoka, Pareidolia may have caused her move or at least helped it along.

There was a marked change in Ami's behavior after the seventh reset. Up to that point she was manipulative and would bluff violence, but she never actually did the evil stuff that became commonplace after the reset. This started with the "Right as Rain" rape of Maya, though there are still mysteries about how real it was and where it fits in the timeline. Pareidolia and/or Ghost Sekai may have been involved as well.

Her tormenting of Maya, including treating her as subhuman, is a massive change from what we've seen before. Compare to what she promised earlier in the chapter:

Obviously she could have been lying, but I think Selebus had a motive beyond dramatic irony when he chose to put such a specifically-worded statement in the game.

On the other hand, Pareidolia (and Sekai) despise Maya, and would love what Ami's putting her through now.


(Sure looks like Ami hears Sekai here.)

To summarize: Ami has hinted at making a sacrifice to protect Sensei from God(s). A god leaves Sensei's head, and at the same time Ami starts doing uncharacteristic things that the same god would want (whether or not she knows it). It's circumstantial, but I think these two changes are linked by her sacrifice.
A little while after the reset, Narrator Ami makes another appearance to talk about how she's going mad because of her worm. There's a new development this time, though: Sensei is apparently pure, and Ami needs to prevent her worm from getting to him.
(This is in Karin's event "A Trip to Uzbekistan")

Possibly she's saying that Sensei's worm (Pareidolia) is gone because of her sacrifice, and she needs to keep things that way. (An alternative worth mentioning: Sensei, the "half-eaten replica", has been corrupted by his worm, but she's trying to protect the "real Akira", whatever that means for her.)

How I interpret some other things in this passage:
- "Every day I slip closer to Him": Note the capitalized Him, which isn't repeated when she talks about Sensei. She's saying she's slipping closer to God, which is what's driving her mad (or vice versa).
- "bed of nails purchased from the bishop's kin": Her mind is rotting, and meanwhile her body is engaging in "sin" because of a transaction she made with (an agent of) God.
- "worm torn from bodies past": Her worm may have come from Sekai (the one which drove her mad before her death) and was either planted or woken up when she read Sekai's poem in "My Life With You".
- "I can hear salvation come": God arrives to interrupt her narration.
I mostly covered this in my last post, but it's worth emphasizing again the contradictions in Ami's behavior. Even after the seventh reset, she was able to rant about how much she hates the gods for her mother's death (in "Shiritori", shown at the start of this post). And yet, her actions seem to support everything that Pareidolia/USER3 wants - most recently and most obviously in pushing Sensei to rape Karin and become the Collector. This is another reason to suspect that there are different Amis in control at different times.
That's what I have so far. Maybe this gives some answers about the Ami situation, but there's still a lot that's left unexplained. Some things I'm thinking about:
- Why would Ami sacrifice herself for this particular Sensei when she regards him as replaceable? She could be bluffing, but I don't think so.

And for good uncles only:

- What exactly does it mean for Ami to offer herself to be "consumed" by God? She used the same word to describe Sekai going mad, and we know from narration that her mind is deteriorating, but she's not acting liking a typical crazy person. It seems like USER3 is influencing her, but how exactly?

- How do the clues about two different Amis fit into all this? I really doubt that Evil Ami is USER3 seizing direct control of her or anything. So why is she here and how does it relate to Ami's sacrifice?

- Who saved Sensei in the sixth reset? He was going to be reset as punishment for not raping anyone, but someone made a sacrifice to save him. Up to now I had assumed that Maya Prime sacrificed herself when she saw that the reset was going wrong, but maybe Ami is actually responsible. After all, Maya was blindsided by the reset, but Ami knew exactly what was going to happen well in advance - including Maya's death and Sensei's catatonia (she wrote a poem about it for Wakana's contest).

- When exactly did Ami make her sacrifice? Around the sixth reset seems the most likely, but then why did the biggest changes not happen until the seventh reset? Or maybe she made multiple bargains with God(s) and I'm getting them confused.

- If Ami sacrificed herself to get Pareidolia out of Sensei's head, why is he now in Yumi's head instead of (or in addition to?) Ami's?

- Is Pareidolia the real USER3? This is something I've been second-guessing for a while. A couple of reasons to doubt it related to this post:
1. Ami knew in advance what would happen in the sixth reset but Pareidolia was convinced Sensei was doomed. Similarly, Pareidolia was clueless about Yumi's TSS.
2. In Della the worm feeds off of the connection to God, but it isn't God himself - Ami even says it blocks the path to God. Pareidolia seems to be Sensei's worm.
If I had to guess at this moment, gun to my head, my leading theory of many possibilities is that Pareidolia is a part of USER3 - or maybe a reflection - which USER3 managed to plant inside of Sensei's head. Thus it acts like USER3, but the real USER3 is elsewhere doing things without Pareidolia's knowledge.

I have my eye on two entities as closely connected to the USER3 puzzle: SeKaori and the still-mysterious Apollo, Peerless God of Dolor.

Beginning of Chapter 4
spoilers.html:
Chapter 4 starts with Sensei mentally broken after Maya's death. Ami recognizes that this leaves him vulnerable and warns him about letting gods in.

It's only a couple of events later that she floats the hypothetical of her sacrifice. If necessary, she'll act to prevent the gods driving Sensei mad.

The contrast between these two is interesting. I'm thinking Ami realizes that she's being manipulated, but is so desperate that she chooses to believe it anyway. Or maybe she's already made a bargain with God at this point, and being with Sensei is supposed to be her reward.

spoilers.title: Della
spoilers.html:
Ami believed that Maya's "death" would change everything, that Sensei would stay inside with her forever. Instead, after he comes out of his catatonia, he goes right back to ignoring Ami in favor of being a manwhore. Ami has a breakdown and blames his behavior on God.

"Della" begins with a narrator, who I assume is Narrator Ami, telling a very strange story about "worms" inside of us which grow when we talk to God.

Ami rants about how Sensei doesn't act the way she wants him to, and comes to the conclusion that he's doing this because of his own worm - talking to God has made him like this. To get him back to "normal", she has to get rid of his worm.

Along with her rant, Ami mixes in lines from "The Gift of the Magi", because she identifies with a girl who sells a part of herself for the benefit of the man she loves. She is "selling" part of herself to God.

And because of that, she's now being eaten by a worm of her own. A worm that makes her act like a bad girl, when we all know that Ami is the best niece ever. Ami is the only girl I will ever need!

spoilers.title: Recovery after Della and the seventh reset
spoilers.html:
After "Della" it's Ami's turn to retreat to her room to recover from a traumatic experience/mental health episode. But while she does superficially get better, Narrator Ami suggests that her mind is continuing to deteriorate. Her worm is making her worse.

She leaves the house for the first time to go on the camping trip, where she has heart-to-heart with Sensei and shares a new outlook on God.

I'm speculating here, but I think Ami is able to catch a second wind because she reaches a state of acceptance. It's like a terminal patient who has a brief recovery shortly before things take a permanent turn for the worse. Ami had been fighting God's influence, especially after she blamed her worm for hurting Sensei in Della. But by the time of the camping trip, she now regards her worm as necessary suffering, a test from God that she must persevere through.

That brings us to seventh reset. Pareidolia abruptly leaves Sensei's head, claiming that he's sacrificed himself, though he conveniently can't remember why.

How likely is it that Pareidolia, an amoral hedonist, would make a selfless sacrifice? Maybe he's trying to claim credit for Ami's sacrifice?

Regardless, Pareidolia has "parting gifts" before he leaves, and it's implied that one of them is sending Nodoka to the world where Sensei and Makoto end up during the reset (side note: I assume this is Ami's wish world). This disturbs the "happy ending" of that world's Ami and activates her murder hobo mode.

I've speculated that Evil Ami came to Sensei's world from this happy ending. (I was wrong about a payoff coming in the eighth reset, but otherwise I still stand by that post.) By sending Nodoka, Pareidolia may have caused her move or at least helped it along.

There was a marked change in Ami's behavior after the seventh reset. Up to that point she was manipulative and would bluff violence, but she never actually did the evil stuff that became commonplace after the reset. This started with the "Right as Rain" rape of Maya, though there are still mysteries about how real it was and where it fits in the timeline. Pareidolia and/or Ghost Sekai may have been involved as well.

Her tormenting of Maya, including treating her as subhuman, is a massive change from what we've seen before. Compare to what she promised earlier in the chapter:

Obviously she could have been lying, but I think Selebus had a motive beyond dramatic irony when he chose to put such a specifically-worded statement in the game.

On the other hand, Pareidolia (and Sekai) despise Maya, and would love what Ami's putting her through now.


(Sure looks like Ami hears Sekai here.)

To summarize: Ami has hinted at making a sacrifice to protect Sensei from God(s). A god leaves Sensei's head, and at the same time Ami starts doing uncharacteristic things that the same god would want (whether or not she knows it). It's circumstantial, but I think these two changes are linked by her sacrifice.

spoilers.title: Narrator Ami gives an update on the worm(s)
spoilers.html:
A little while after the reset, Narrator Ami makes another appearance to talk about how she's going mad because of her worm. There's a new development this time, though: Sensei is apparently pure, and Ami needs to prevent her worm from getting to him.
(This is in Karin's event "A Trip to Uzbekistan")

Possibly she's saying that Sensei's worm (Pareidolia) is gone because of her sacrifice, and she needs to keep things that way. (An alternative worth mentioning: Sensei, the "half-eaten replica", has been corrupted by his worm, but she's trying to protect the "real Akira", whatever that means for her.)

How I interpret some other things in this passage:
- "Every day I slip closer to Him": Note the capitalized Him, which isn't repeated when she talks about Sensei. She's saying she's slipping closer to God, which is what's driving her mad (or vice versa).
- "bed of nails purchased from the bishop's kin": Her mind is rotting, and meanwhile her body is engaging in "sin" because of a transaction she made with (an agent of) God.
- "worm torn from bodies past": Her worm may have come from Sekai (the one which drove her mad before her death) and was either planted or woken up when she read Sekai's poem in "My Life With You".
- "I can hear salvation come": God arrives to interrupt her narration.

spoilers.title: Open questions
spoilers.html:
- Why would Ami sacrifice herself for this particular Sensei when she regards him as replaceable? She could be bluffing, but I don't think so.

And for good uncles only:

- What exactly does it mean for Ami to offer herself to be "consumed" by God? She used the same word to describe Sekai going mad, and we know from narration that her mind is deteriorating, but she's not acting liking a typical crazy person. It seems like USER3 is influencing her, but how exactly?

Up to now I had assumed that Maya Prime sacrificed herself when she saw that the reset was going wrong, but maybe Ami is actually responsible. After all, Maya was blindsided by the reset, but Ami knew exactly what was going to happen well in advance - including Maya's death and Sensei's catatonia (she wrote a poem about it for Wakana's contest).

- If Ami sacrificed herself to get Pareidolia out of Sensei's head, why is he now in Yumi's head instead of (or in addition to?) Ami's?

- "bed of nails purchased from the bishop's kin": Her mind is rotting, and meanwhile her body is engaging in "sin" because of a transaction she made with (an agent of) God.
- "worm torn from bodies past": Her worm may have come from Sekai (the one which drove her mad before her death) and was either planted or woken up when she read Sekai's poem in "My Life With You".
- "I can hear salvation come": God arrives to interrupt her narration.

spoilers.title: Recent events
spoilers.html: I mostly covered this in my last post, but it's worth emphasizing again the contradictions in Ami's behavior. Even after the seventh reset, she was able to rant about how much she hates the gods for her mother's death (in "Shiritori", shown at the start of this post). And yet, her actions seem to support everything that Pareidolia/USER3 wants - most recently and most obviously in pushing Sensei to rape Karin and become the Collector. This is another reason to suspect that there are different Amis in control at different times.

spoilers.title: Open questions
spoilers.html:
- Why would Ami sacrifice herself for this particular Sensei when she regards him as replaceable? She could be bluffing, but I don't think so.
View attachment 5846576
And for good uncles only:
View attachment 5846559

- What exactly does it mean for Ami to offer herself to be "consumed" by God? She used the same word to describe Sekai going mad, and we know from narration that her mind is deteriorating, but she's not acting liking a typical crazy person. It seems like USER3 is influencing her, but how exactly?

- How do the clues about two different Amis fit into all this? I really doubt that Evil Ami is USER3 seizing direct control of her or anything. So why is she here and how does it relate to Ami's sacrifice?

- Who saved Sensei in the sixth reset? He was going to be reset as punishment for not raping anyone, but someone made a sacrifice to save him. Up to now I had assumed that Maya Prime sacrificed herself when she saw that the reset was going wrong, but maybe Ami is actually responsible. After all, Maya was blindsided by the reset, but Ami knew exactly what was going to happen well in advance - including Maya's death and Sensei's catatonia (she wrote a poem about it for Wakana's contest).

- When exactly did Ami make her sacrifice? Around the sixth reset seems the most likely, but then why did the biggest changes not happen until the seventh reset? Or maybe she made multiple bargains with God(s) and I'm getting them confused.

- If Ami sacrificed herself to get Pareidolia out of Sensei's head, why is he now in Yumi's head instead of (or in addition to?) Ami's?

- Is Pareidolia the real USER3? This is something I've been second-guessing for a while. A couple of reasons to doubt it related to this post:
1. Ami knew in advance what would happen in the sixth reset but Pareidolia was convinced Sensei was doomed. Similarly, Pareidolia was clueless about Yumi's TSS.
2. In Della the worm feeds off of the connection to God, but it isn't God himself - Ami even says it blocks the path to God. Pareidolia seems to be Sensei's worm.
If I had to guess at this moment, gun to my head, my leading theory of many possibilities is that Pareidolia is a part of USER3 - or maybe a reflection - which USER3 managed to plant inside of Sensei's head. Thus it acts like USER3, but the real USER3 is elsewhere doing things without Pareidolia's knowledge.

I have my eye on two entities as closely connected to the USER3 puzzle: SeKaori and the still-mysterious Apollo, Peerless God of Dolor.

Fanfest is dumb. Now that I've shared my nuanced opinion, let's get to the theorycrafting.

Theory: Pareidolia isn't in Sensei's head anymore because Ami sacrificed herself to get rid of him.
I think there is fairly good evidence (though not conclusive) that Ami offered herself as a sacrifice in a belief that it would protect Sensei from unspecified God(s). The Pareidolia part doesn't come from direct evidence, but rather by looking at timing along with the hints that Pareidolia/USER3 is involved in what's currently happening to Ami. I wrote about that in my last Ami post, here:

I still don't have a complete theory for what's going on with Ami, this post is just about tying together some of the evidence. I've been pretty thorough in posting everything I have noticed, not knowing what bits will be most relevant. So I apologize in advance if this post feels a bit scattershot.
After the Nakayarakawayama beach trip, Ami yells at Sensei about two things:
1. She does things for Sensei that he doesn't know about.
2. She refuses to let Sensei be driven mad by the gods, the way that her mom was.
View attachment 5846585 View attachment 5846586
Two lines later:
View attachment 5846567 View attachment 5846569 View attachment 5846570
N.B.: She says "I will not lose you" instead of "I don't want to lose you." She's trying to prevent it.
I believe that these are connected, that what Sensei is unaware of is that Ami has been protecting him from God(s) (most likely USER3/Pareidolia). Early in Chapter 4, Ami told us how she would do it: by sacrificing herself and allowing the gods to "consume" her in his place.
View attachment 5846581 View attachment 5846582
Over the course of Chapter 4, Ami has hinted at her relationship with God(s), which has changed over time in tandem with her worsening mental state. In chronological order:
Chapter 4 starts with Sensei mentally broken after Maya's death. Ami recognizes that this leaves him vulnerable and warns him about letting gods in.
View attachment 5846556 View attachment 5846557
It's only a couple of events later that she floats the hypothetical of her sacrifice. If necessary, she'll act to prevent the gods driving Sensei mad.

In contrast, she seemingly has a positive view of "God" after Sensei comes out his coma. God told her that they're meant to be together, and she takes him at his word.
View attachment 5846549
The contrast between these two is interesting. I'm thinking Ami realizes that she's being manipulated, but is so desperate that she chooses to believe it anyway. Or maybe she's already made a bargain with God at this point, and being with Sensei is supposed to be her reward.
Ami believed that Maya's "death" would change everything, that Sensei would stay inside with her forever. Instead, after he comes out of his catatonia, he goes right back to ignoring Ami in favor of being a manwhore. Ami has a breakdown and blames his behavior on God.

"Della" begins with a narrator, who I assume is Narrator Ami, telling a very strange story about "worms" inside of us which grow when we talk to God.
View attachment 5846588 View attachment 5846590
Ami rants about how Sensei doesn't act the way she wants him to, and comes to the conclusion that he's doing this because of his own worm - talking to God has made him like this. To get him back to "normal", she has to get rid of his worm.
View attachment 5846551
Along with her rant, Ami mixes in lines from "The Gift of the Magi", because she identifies with a girl who sells a part of herself for the benefit of the man she loves. She is "selling" part of herself to God.
View attachment 5846553
And because of that, she's now being eaten by a worm of her own. A worm that makes her act like a bad girl, when we all know that Ami is the best niece ever. Ami is the only girl I will ever need!
View attachment 5846554 View attachment 5846555
After "Della" it's Ami's turn to retreat to her room to recover from a traumatic experience/mental health episode. But while she does superficially get better, Narrator Ami suggests that her mind is continuing to deteriorate. Her worm is making her worse.
View attachment 5846613 View attachment 5846621 View attachment 5846627
She leaves the house for the first time to go on the camping trip, where she has heart-to-heart with Sensei and shares a new outlook on God.
View attachment 5846578 View attachment 5846579
I'm speculating here, but I think Ami is able to catch a second wind because she reaches a state of acceptance. It's like a terminal patient who has a brief recovery shortly before things take a permanent turn for the worse. Ami had been fighting God's influence, especially after she blamed her worm for hurting Sensei in Della. But by the time of the camping trip, she now regards her worm as necessary suffering, a test from God that she must persevere through.

That brings us to seventh reset. Pareidolia abruptly leaves Sensei's head, claiming that he's sacrificed himself, though he conveniently can't remember why.
View attachment 5846629
How likely is it that Pareidolia, an amoral hedonist, would make a selfless sacrifice? Maybe he's trying to claim credit for Ami's sacrifice?

Regardless, Pareidolia has "parting gifts" before he leaves, and it's implied that one of them is sending Nodoka to the world where Sensei and Makoto end up during the reset (side note: I assume this is Ami's wish world). This disturbs the "happy ending" of that world's Ami and activates her murder hobo mode.
View attachment 5846633 View attachment 5846634 View attachment 5846564
I've speculated that Evil Ami came to Sensei's world from this happy ending. (I was wrong about a payoff coming in the eighth reset, but otherwise I still stand by that post.) By sending Nodoka, Pareidolia may have caused her move or at least helped it along.

There was a marked change in Ami's behavior after the seventh reset. Up to that point she was manipulative and would bluff violence, but she never actually did the evil stuff that became commonplace after the reset. This started with the "Right as Rain" rape of Maya, though there are still mysteries about how real it was and where it fits in the timeline. Pareidolia and/or Ghost Sekai may have been involved as well.

Her tormenting of Maya, including treating her as subhuman, is a massive change from what we've seen before. Compare to what she promised earlier in the chapter:
View attachment 5846562
Obviously she could have been lying, but I think Selebus had a motive beyond dramatic irony when he chose to put such a specifically-worded statement in the game.

On the other hand, Pareidolia (and Sekai) despise Maya, and would love what Ami's putting her through now.
View attachment 5846738
View attachment 5846630 View attachment 5846631
(Sure looks like Ami hears Sekai here.)

To summarize: Ami has hinted at making a sacrifice to protect Sensei from God(s). A god leaves Sensei's head, and at the same time Ami starts doing uncharacteristic things that the same god would want (whether or not she knows it). It's circumstantial, but I think these two changes are linked by her sacrifice.
A little while after the reset, Narrator Ami makes another appearance to talk about how she's going mad because of her worm. There's a new development this time, though: Sensei is apparently pure, and Ami needs to prevent her worm from getting to him.
(This is in Karin's event "A Trip to Uzbekistan")
View attachment 5846628
Possibly she's saying that Sensei's worm (Pareidolia) is gone because of her sacrifice, and she needs to keep things that way. (An alternative worth mentioning: Sensei, the "half-eaten replica", has been corrupted by his worm, but she's trying to protect the "real Akira", whatever that means for her.)

How I interpret some other things in this passage:
- "Every day I slip closer to Him": Note the capitalized Him, which isn't repeated when she talks about Sensei. She's saying she's slipping closer to God, which is what's driving her mad (or vice versa).
- "bed of nails purchased from the bishop's kin": Her mind is rotting, and meanwhile her body is engaging in "sin" because of a transaction she made with (an agent of) God.
- "worm torn from bodies past": Her worm may have come from Sekai (the one which drove her mad before her death) and was either planted or woken up when she read Sekai's poem in "My Life With You".
- "I can hear salvation come": God arrives to interrupt her narration.
I mostly covered this in my last post, but it's worth emphasizing again the contradictions in Ami's behavior. Even after the seventh reset, she was able to rant about how much she hates the gods for her mother's death (in "Shiritori", shown at the start of this post). And yet, her actions seem to support everything that Pareidolia/USER3 wants - most recently and most obviously in pushing Sensei to rape Karin and become the Collector. This is another reason to suspect that there are different Amis in control at different times.
That's what I have so far. Maybe this gives some answers about the Ami situation, but there's still a lot that's left unexplained. Some things I'm thinking about:
- Why would Ami sacrifice herself for this particular Sensei when she regards him as replaceable? She could be bluffing, but I don't think so.
View attachment 5846576
And for good uncles only:
View attachment 5846559

- What exactly does it mean for Ami to offer herself to be "consumed" by God? She used the same word to describe Sekai going mad, and we know from narration that her mind is deteriorating, but she's not acting liking a typical crazy person. It seems like USER3 is influencing her, but how exactly?

- How do the clues about two different Amis fit into all this? I really doubt that Evil Ami is USER3 seizing direct control of her or anything. So why is she here and how does it relate to Ami's sacrifice?

- Who saved Sensei in the sixth reset? He was going to be reset as punishment for not raping anyone, but someone made a sacrifice to save him. Up to now I had assumed that Maya Prime sacrificed herself when she saw that the reset was going wrong, but maybe Ami is actually responsible. After all, Maya was blindsided by the reset, but Ami knew exactly what was going to happen well in advance - including Maya's death and Sensei's catatonia (she wrote a poem about it for Wakana's contest).

- When exactly did Ami make her sacrifice? Around the sixth reset seems the most likely, but then why did the biggest changes not happen until the seventh reset? Or maybe she made multiple bargains with God(s) and I'm getting them confused.

- If Ami sacrificed herself to get Pareidolia out of Sensei's head, why is he now in Yumi's head instead of (or in addition to?) Ami's?

- Is Pareidolia the real USER3? This is something I've been second-guessing for a while. A couple of reasons to doubt it related to this post:
1. Ami knew in advance what would happen in the sixth reset but Pareidolia was convinced Sensei was doomed. Similarly, Pareidolia was clueless about Yumi's TSS.
2. In Della the worm feeds off of the connection to God, but it isn't God himself - Ami even says it blocks the path to God. Pareidolia seems to be Sensei's worm.
If I had to guess at this moment, gun to my head, my leading theory of many possibilities is that Pareidolia is a part of USER3 - or maybe a reflection - which USER3 managed to plant inside of Sensei's head. Thus it acts like USER3, but the real USER3 is elsewhere doing things without Pareidolia's knowledge.

I have my eye on two entities as closely connected to the USER3 puzzle: SeKaori and the still-mysterious Apollo, Peerless God of Dolor.
Click to expand...
I have finally finished my fourth full re-read of LiL just yesterday and am currently working on a separate extensive post on the less prevalent mysteries that were brought up over the course of the last ten or so updates (since I feel like many of them were kind of mostly ignored by a decent chunk of people here, either due to the general rising dissatisfaction with the quality of the game ever since the previous Fanfest, resulting in a lesser level of engagement with the narrative overall, or as an unfortunate consequence of the hyper-specific focus on everything surrounding Ami, Maya and the Wishing Well after the major 0.53 reveals), so I might touch upon this particular topic in greater detail there, since I was planning to include a separate section on the Gods and the Trinity anyway, but speaking of Ami and “Right as Rain”:

What about the strange heart-shaped smiling-face entity that briefly appears at the very end of that event, narrating that “In this world, it’s you and me – everyone else is noise. And the longer you listen to it, the less sense it makes” and calling itself “the ghost of better days”? I know that there were (and still debatably are) a lot of reasons to suspect that this entity is most likely Sekai – the “ghost of better days” line especially strongly points towards her – but could it instead be some abstract manifestation of Ami Prime that metaphorically and/or physically “replaces” the original Ami (since the original Ami “dies”, just like Maya, as per that same narration), causing her notable shift in behavior after the seventh Reset?

I say this because, to my knowledge, Sekai never really mentions anything about being any more “real” than anyone else in all of her ideological ramblings, whereas Ami – *especially* post-fifth-Halloween Ami – has always been very insistent on treating everyone other than herself and Sensei as “lesser beings”: from her relationship with the Nu Maya (whom she calls a “fake” and a “living doll”), to a lot of what she says in “Victrola” and “A Vivid Explosion of Color” about being “the main heroine” and “the true protagonist of this story”. “Victrola” in particular is very interesting, as (according to the wiki) missing this event replaces it with “INESCAPABLE WHITE NOISE” – yet another reference to “noise”, the same as the aforementioned mysterious entity.

Also, I know that LiL is not Homestuck, and so the unique “written speech patterns” are not at all an easy and surefire way to determine the speaker’s identity – especially since we have a confirmation that it is possible to fake them *and* know that the Trinity are all inherently aspects of one single divine being – but typing in bold (outside of generally being used for the sake of strong emphasis) seems to be most consistently associated with Ami out of all characters: she does this on multiple occasions throughout the fifth Halloween event chain, like in “Wake Up (My Story)” (when she says the titular “THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE MY STORY”) or “Pop Goes the Weasel” (while she is killing Nodoka); she also does it a few times in “Rain King” (when telling Sensei “don’t open the door” or screaming how she “CAN’T TAKE IT ANYMORE”); and if that one piece of narration in “A Trip to Uzbekistan” was also made by her, like aramaug suggests, then she does it there, as well. Plus, aside from Ami, I genuinely struggle to think of a single other narrator who has repeatedly expressed themselves through bold text, since most of them just speak normally, use regular cursive, or otherwise employ some variation of upper/lower-case writing style with differing levels of punctuation. Just bold text, though? *That* is pretty unique.

spoilers.title: Recovery after Della and the seventh reset
spoilers.html:
After "Della" it's Ami's turn to retreat to her room to recover from a traumatic experience/mental health episode. But while she does superficially get better, Narrator Ami suggests that her mind is continuing to deteriorate. Her worm is making her worse.
View attachment 5846613 View attachment 5846621 View attachment 5846627
She leaves the house for the first time to go on the camping trip, where she has heart-to-heart with Sensei and shares a new outlook on God.
View attachment 5846578 View attachment 5846579
I'm speculating here, but I think Ami is able to catch a second wind because she reaches a state of acceptance. It's like a terminal patient who has a brief recovery shortly before things take a permanent turn for the worse. Ami had been fighting God's influence, especially after she blamed her worm for hurting Sensei in Della. But by the time of the camping trip, she now regards her worm as necessary suffering, a test from God that she must persevere through.

That brings us to seventh reset. Pareidolia abruptly leaves Sensei's head, claiming that he's sacrificed himself, though he conveniently can't remember why.
View attachment 5846629
How likely is it that Pareidolia, an amoral hedonist, would make a selfless sacrifice? Maybe he's trying to claim credit for Ami's sacrifice?

Regardless, Pareidolia has "parting gifts" before he leaves, and it's implied that one of them is sending Nodoka to the world where Sensei and Makoto end up during the reset (side note: I assume this is Ami's wish world). This disturbs the "happy ending" of that world's Ami and activates her murder hobo mode.
View attachment 5846633 View attachment 5846634 View attachment 5846564
I've speculated that Evil Ami came to Sensei's world from this happy ending. (I was wrong about a payoff coming in the eighth reset, but otherwise I still stand by that post.) By sending Nodoka, Pareidolia may have caused her move or at least helped it along.

There was a marked change in Ami's behavior after the seventh reset. Up to that point she was manipulative and would bluff violence, but she never actually did the evil stuff that became commonplace after the reset. This started with the "Right as Rain" rape of Maya, though there are still mysteries about how real it was and where it fits in the timeline. Pareidolia and/or Ghost Sekai may have been involved as well.

Her tormenting of Maya, including treating her as subhuman, is a massive change from what we've seen before. Compare to what she promised earlier in the chapter:
View attachment 5846562
Obviously she could have been lying, but I think Selebus had a motive beyond dramatic irony when he chose to put such a specifically-worded statement in the game.

On the other hand, Pareidolia (and Sekai) despise Maya, and would love what Ami's putting her through now.
View attachment 5846738
View attachment 5846630 View attachment 5846631
(Sure looks like Ami hears Sekai here.)

To summarize: Ami has hinted at making a sacrifice to protect Sensei from God(s). A god leaves Sensei's head, and at the same time Ami starts doing uncharacteristic things that the same god would want (whether or not she knows it). It's circumstantial, but I think these two changes are linked by her sacrifice.

spoilers.title: Narrator Ami gives an update on the worm(s)
spoilers.html:
A little while after the reset, Narrator Ami makes another appearance to talk about how she's going mad because of her worm. There's a new development this time, though: Sensei is apparently pure, and Ami needs to prevent her worm from getting to him.
(This is in Karin's event "A Trip to Uzbekistan")
View attachment 5846628
Possibly she's saying that Sensei's worm (Pareidolia) is gone because of her sacrifice, and she needs to keep things that way. (An alternative worth mentioning: Sensei, the "half-eaten replica", has been corrupted by his worm, but she's trying to protect the "real Akira", whatever that means for her.)

How I interpret some other things in this passage:
- "Every day I slip closer to Him": Note the capitalized Him, which isn't repeated when she talks about Sensei. She's saying she's slipping closer to God, which is what's driving her mad (or vice versa).
- "bed of nails purchased from the bishop's kin": Her mind is rotting, and meanwhile her body is engaging in "sin" because of a transaction she made with (an agent of) God.
- "worm torn from bodies past": Her worm may have come from Sekai (the one which drove her mad before her death) and was either planted or woken up when she read Sekai's poem in "My Life With You".
- "I can hear salvation come": God arrives to interrupt her narration.

spoilers.html: I mostly covered this in my last post, but it's worth emphasizing again the contradictions in Ami's behavior. Even after the seventh reset, she was able to rant about how much she hates the gods for her mother's death (in "Shiritori", shown at the start of this post). And yet, her actions seem to support everything that Pareidolia/USER3 wants - most recently and most obviously in pushing Sensei to rape Karin and become the Collector. This is another reason to suspect that there are different Amis in control at different times.

spoilers.title: Open questions
spoilers.html:
- Why would Ami sacrifice herself for this particular Sensei when she regards him as replaceable? She could be bluffing, but I don't think so.
View attachment 5846576
And for good uncles only:
View attachment 5846559

- What exactly does it mean for Ami to offer herself to be "consumed" by God? She used the same word to describe Sekai going mad, and we know from narration that her mind is deteriorating, but she's not acting liking a typical crazy person. It seems like USER3 is influencing her, but how exactly?

- How do the clues about two different Amis fit into all this? I really doubt that Evil Ami is USER3 seizing direct control of her or anything. So why is she here and how does it relate to Ami's sacrifice?

- Who saved Sensei in the sixth reset? He was going to be reset as punishment for not raping anyone, but someone made a sacrifice to save him. Up to now I had assumed that Maya Prime sacrificed herself when she saw that the reset was going wrong, but maybe Ami is actually responsible. After all, Maya was blindsided by the reset, but Ami knew exactly what was going to happen well in advance - including Maya's death and Sensei's catatonia (she wrote a poem about it for Wakana's contest).

- When exactly did Ami make her sacrifice? Around the sixth reset seems the most likely, but then why did the biggest changes not happen until the seventh reset? Or maybe she made multiple bargains with God(s) and I'm getting them confused.

- If Ami sacrificed herself to get Pareidolia out of Sensei's head, why is he now in Yumi's head instead of (or in addition to?) Ami's?

- Is Pareidolia the real USER3? This is something I've been second-guessing for a while. A couple of reasons to doubt it related to this post:
1. Ami knew in advance what would happen in the sixth reset but Pareidolia was convinced Sensei was doomed. Similarly, Pareidolia was clueless about Yumi's TSS.
2. In Della the worm feeds off of the connection to God, but it isn't God himself - Ami even says it blocks the path to God. Pareidolia seems to be Sensei's worm.
If I had to guess at this moment, gun to my head, my leading theory of many possibilities is that Pareidolia is a part of USER3 - or maybe a reflection - which USER3 managed to plant inside of Sensei's head. Thus it acts like USER3, but the real USER3 is elsewhere doing things without Pareidolia's knowledge.

I have my eye on two entities as closely connected to the USER3 puzzle: SeKaori and the still-mysterious Apollo, Peerless God of Dolor.

spoilers.title: Ami is so cute
spoilers.html:
What about the strange heart-shaped smiling-face entity that briefly appears at the very end of that event, narrating that “In this world, it’s you and me – everyone else is noise. And the longer you listen to it, the less sense it makes” and calling itself “the ghost of better days”? I know that there were (and still debatably are) a lot of reasons to suspect that this entity is most likely Sekai – the “ghost of better days” line especially strongly points towards her – but could it instead be some abstract manifestation of Ami Prime that metaphorically and/or physically “replaces” the original Ami (since the original Ami “dies”, just like Maya, as per that same narration), causing her notable shift in behavior after the seventh Reset?

I say this because, to my knowledge, Sekai never really mentions anything about being any more “real” than anyone else in all of her ideological ramblings, whereas Ami – *especially* post-fifth-Halloween Ami – has always been very insistent on treating everyone other than herself and Sensei as “lesser beings”: from her relationship with the Nu Maya (whom she calls a “fake” and a “living doll”), to a lot of what she says in “Victrola” and “A Vivid Explosion of Color” about being “the main heroine” and “the true protagonist of this story”. “Victrola” in particular is very interesting, as (according to the wiki) missing this event replaces it with “INESCAPABLE WHITE NOISE” – yet another reference to “noise”, the same as the aforementioned mysterious entity.

Also, I know that LiL is not Homestuck, and so the unique “written speech patterns” are not at all an easy and surefire way to determine the speaker’s identity – especially since we have a confirmation that it is possible to fake them *and* know that the Trinity are all inherently aspects of one single divine being – but typing in bold (outside of generally being used for the sake of strong emphasis) seems to be most consistently associated with Ami out of all characters: she does this on multiple occasions throughout the fifth Halloween event chain, like in “Wake Up (My Story)” (when she says the titular “THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE MY STORY”) or “Pop Goes the Weasel” (while she is killing Nodoka); she also does it a few times in “Rain King” (when telling Sensei “don’t open the door” or screaming how she “CAN’T TAKE IT ANYMORE”); and if that one piece of narration in “A Trip to Uzbekistan” was also made by her, like aramaug suggests, then she does it there, as well. Plus, aside from Ami, I genuinely struggle to think of a single other narrator who has repeatedly expressed themselves through bold text, since most of them just speak normally, use regular cursive, or otherwise employ some variation of upper/lower-case writing style with differing levels of punctuation. Just bold text, though? *That* is pretty unique.

posts.content_html_raw:
How are yall doing? First time poster here. I have to get this off my chest.

I know this is going to come out of left field but Yasu's karaoke song during the christmas event hit me like a ton of bricks. I have to express how much i love this piece. Sure she was raspy and the melody, although nice, isnt overly complex . Nonetheless, that song she sang was one of the most beautiful things i ever heard. It was moving because her performance captured her innocense, insecurities, pain, another side of her (compared to her usual zealot rhetoric), passion, and desperation as she cries through her whispers. It was also catchy. I heard all of this and i didnt understand a single word she said but the vibe and the emotions chilled my soul to its core. It brought me to tears. I felt her pain. I felt her happiness. It was so moving i had to share my passion on a porno forum for gamers.

We all know Yasu's singing has its imperfections, but thats what makes it so raw. As most of you remember, the great Edgar Allen Poe once said, “There is no exquisite beauty… without some strangeness in the proportion.”

With that, is there a way to export this song from the game files? I WANT this song. NO I NEED this song.

Hello, first time posting.

I wanted to speak about Sana and get some other perspectives.
In this uptade, Sana said she'll be with Akira forever. I keep thinking back to the reset, where we saw Akira living alone with older Sana still visiting him (not sure if that's set in the future, but it feels significant). She was also someone we saw during Akira ans Ayane perfect life, so i wonder if her forever have more weight ?

There's also the fact that at one point Sana couldn't say she loved him ( that she sees him more like an object, for her urge ? ). So when she says it back in this update, is that genuine, or is she performing what she thinks she's supposed to say?

On top of that, she's the poster girl for Chapter 4, which has to mean something for her arc going forward.

As for Sarah, I found it really strange that she didn't bring up Sana at all when Akira opened up about his issues with Ami. She also never directly confronted him about what she witnessed? I think Sarah might blame herself more, either for the situation itself, or for the way she raised Sana.

Apologies to Bingoogus, but this is such a bizarre claim to me. If I restrict myself to Chapter 4, I see Sana as the game's weakest character because she's completely lacking in nuance. All her thoughts seem to originate from "what's the best way to manipulate people so that I'm the one who gets Sensei's dick", with literally nothing else mattering. There's no sign that she cares anymore about any of her friendships or is capable of feeling empathy for anyone else.

And it's even weirder to view her as a "compelling love interest". What's compelling about someone completely lacking in positive qualities? Would anyone seriously want to spend time around this person, even if you're the object of her obsession? Okay fine, she's a sexual freak, but does that really speak for her as a love interest?

Apologies to Bingoogus, but this is such a bizarre claim to me. If I restrict myself to Chapter 4, I see Sana as the game's weakest character because she's completely lacking in nuance. All her thoughts seem to originate from "what's the best way to manipulate people so that I'm the one who gets Sensei's dick", with literally nothing else mattering. There's no sign that she cares anymore about any of her friendships or is capable of feeling empathy for anyone else.

And it's even weirder to view her as a "compelling love interest". What's compelling about someone completely lacking in positive qualities? Would anyone seriously want to spend time around this person, even if you're the object of her obsession? Okay fine, she's a sexual freak, but does that really speak for her as a love interest?
Click to expand...
I mean, this is ultimately a matter of individual opinions and whatnot, so if you personally find Chapter 4 Sana to be completely bland and boring, then that’s totally fair, but I, for example, completely disagree with the perspective that "there's no sign that [Sana] cares anymore about any of her friendships or is capable of feeling empathy for anyone else": there is a whole section in my recent essay on the theme of love in LiL dedicated to refuting exactly that.

To quickly reiterate my main point from that post, I basically argued that Sana *is* perfectly capable of feeling empathy and *does* genuinely care about the people closest to her (most notably Akira and Sara) – it's just that her way of showing those feelings got incredibly twisted as the result of her HOPE-induced "callous" awakening, and that inherent dichotomy between sincere love and unashamed depravity (in addition to how Sana's mask of perceived innocence changes from a passive defense tool to a weapon she now actively uses to her advantage) is exactly what makes her so interesting and compelling in my eyes (and, I would argue, Selebus' eyes too, judging by his statements about her). Not to mention that if Sana truly *did* only care about "getting Sensei's dick", then she wouldn't be so hung up on getting him to repeat his love confession and would instead simply enjoy her new life as a "despicable meat toilet", rather than constantly focus on something that doesn't directly pertain to her regularly getting laid: God knows that Akira is perfectly capable of repeatedly boning you into oblivion even without mutual feelings of "love", so that is not at all a prerequisite if your only two worries are "sex" and "more sex".

As for "What's compelling about someone completely lacking in positive qualities?", the interesting thing about life is that "positive qualities" mean different things to different people. I, for instance, consider Sana's commitment to being entirely true to herself regardless of what everyone else thinks of her (something that she openly vocalizes to Sara in "The Puppeteer") to be a very positive quality, even if it makes her an awful human being from a moral standpoint. It also works the other way, too: if you're someone who is just as depraved and twisted as she is – or, hell, maybe even more – Sana would be one of the last people on the planet to ever take issue with that, so you wouldn't have to worry about constantly wearing a mask in front of her, which is a major plus in a romantic partner. And, finally, credit where credit's due: the girl is surprisingly cunning and resourceful when she actually chooses to apply herself, so she has that going for her, as well.

So, yeah, there are multiple reasons to like Sana, both as a character and as a person. You just personally don't, and that's perfectly okay.

I guess it depends on how exactly do you define “completely revolve around sex”.

Because, sure, I suppose that you *could* boil down all of Sana’s post-0.49 interactions with Sara to just her “trying to manipulate Sara into having sex with Sensei” and then call it a day, but I feel like viewing it through such a simplistic lens is very reductive, as there are also many other, much more subtle themes at play here – themes that are extremely integral to both of the characters involved, but are inevitably going to get overlooked (if not outright dismissed) when you oversimplify the entire conversation to just a single one of its main components.

On Sana’s end, Chapter 4 shows us Sana in her final stages of self-discovery and self-acceptance – going from a passive stance of “preserving the status quo because it’s easier this way”, perfectly exemplified by her triangle metaphor from “Closer to Me” all the way back in Chapter 2, to the complete opposite active stance of “actively taking control of my own life, even if it means having to risk breaking the established comfortable stability in the process” – which is then only further compounded by her character’s second major theme: Chapter 1-3 Sana’s fundamental disconnect between her “inner” and “outer” self. Pretty much everyone around Sana used to constantly impose this fake ideal of an “innocent little angel that could know no sin” onto her, even sometimes going as far as borderline blaming the poor girl for “not living up to their expectations of her own purity”, despite the fact that this is both extremely unrealistic (since no human being is *this* innocent, even more so if they are a teenager) *and* incredibly unhealthy for the person who is the unwilling target of that imposition – something that Sana herself repeatedly brings up in various conversations throughout all of Chapter 4, sharing how much happier she is now that this “disconnect” has been finally eliminated (due to the girl completely shattering her previous image and then rebuilding it anew in accordance with her own wishes), since people no longer treat her like a holy virgin who has no idea where babies come from.

And on Sara’s end, we have an insane triple combo of her personal complex of inadequacy as a parent (caused by a combination of how Sara herself was abused by her own family, resulting in a subconscious desire to “always try to do better than them”, and her inner repressed feelings of shame due how easy and desperate for sex and affection she has always been), her deep-rooted loneliness as a woman who desperately wants to be loved and cared for by a worthy man of her choosing (since the original one hit it and quit it, so Sara never got to experience a “proper” married life as a wife, instead spending her best years struggling for even a piece of happiness as a single mom), and also Sara’s still unresolved trauma of losing Shota that she keeps continually running away from, making the woman that much more protective of her only remaining child, even when that protectiveness reaches into the ”overbearing” territory.

*All of this* is directly relevant to properly understanding the full complexity of every single character interaction between Sana and Sara post-second Nodokathon, since they themselves repeatedly bring up these subjects (both to each other and when talking to Akira) over the course of their last few character events – "The Puppeteer" and their 0.57 most recent ones in particular. And to reduce this entire intricate clusterfuck of a mother-daughter relationship to something as simple and clear-cut as “Sana wants to fuck Sensei, and she also wants Sara to fuck him together with her”, while not *completely* inaccurate, is… not exactly a reading of the text that I can agree with, I’m sorry.

I’ve pretty much said my piece already, so if you're still not convinced that there is more to Sana than just “sex, sex, sex”, then I guess we will simply have to respectfully agree to disagree on this point.

Looks like everyone’s negative emotion about Sana, but honestly, I think it’s just because you’re all too focused on Sara’s feelings.
Let me throw out a somewhat crazy take: in my eyes, everything Sana did was right. Basically, she was just fully living by the idea that “Sometimes, forcing people to do things they’re not comfortable with is the best way to move them forward.”

Sara definitely has a lot of reasons to be upset, since Sana changed way too fast. And she really is like what Akira said: “If you took advantage of her undying love for you and coerced her into it.”

But honestly, what Sana did was the best move for the whole Sakakibaras,she truly has a complete understanding of Sara—it just needed some time. It also shows how much Sana loves Sara. Sana is selfish and comes off as a bad person, but she’s doing the right thing, kinda like Ami—who, of course, also gets a lot of criticism.

Sana really is a shady bitch. But she’s not all about sex like some people think. In the Sana event “Taller,” she and Sensei were just sharing personal feelings. And if you ignore all the sexual stuff, you’ll notice there’s actually a chain of conversations about love. Later, in the lust event “Four Letter Words,” Sana thinks Sensei doesn’t love her—and surprisingly, her intuition’s right again. Sensei loves the Sana from ten years in the future, the Sana who doesn’t put pressure on him and never leaves.
Across these two events of 0.57, Sana’s view on love finally gets fully spelled out. Basically, she believes love means being together forever, eternal companionship.This is what sana will do not only in ten years but the future.



And that’s actually similar to Maya’s situation—another sex addict who went through millions of years of searching.
An eternal companion. That’s why Sana can be the poster girl alongside Ami, Maya,and Ayane. That’s why she’s a love interest.

Not necessarily *your* or *aramaug's* eyes, mind you, but just *someone's* (mine, Selebus', Akira's), as a general refutation of the proposed claim that Sana is "completely lacking in positive qualities" and "would anyone seriously want to spend time around this person?", because people are inherently different, with their own distinct values, beliefs and priorities, and just because *you* look at someone and think "man, what an awful fucking person, I wouldn't want to be with them not in a million years" doesn't mean that there is *no one* who would look at the same person and think "wow, they are perfect – 10/10 girlfriend/boyfriend material".

Ok, so I finished the game for the first time. Honestly, not even really sure what to touch on, but I’ll list a few thoughts that I currently have.

I still think the MC sucks as a character, and I think the game is at its weakest when we throw the same pity party for the MC that’s been thrown a billion times. Like how many times do we need to hear the SAME EXACT conversation:

MC: “wah wah / I’m can’t change myself / I can’t stop myself from assaulting kids / I’m irredeemable trash / wah wah”

Emotional Support Chick: “No Akira, (choose one or a combination)

1) I’m just as bad as you.
2) Mistakes can be fixed.
3) You’ve suffered enough.
4) It’s not your fault due to (trauma).

So, I will do nothing and let you continue to abuse half your class and/or my child.”
Click to expand...
Like I don’t know why we keep getting this scene. There’s no new point being made. And you’re not gonna convince me the MC is sympathetic no matter how many times you say the same thing lol.

Besides that, I think the writing in the later patches has gotten weird. Is it just me, or is like every other line about sex. Maybe this is on purpose – the world is becoming really fucked and everyone is being influenced to just not give a shit anymore or become horny 24/7, but it kind of flanderizes some of the characters where it's not supposed to be their main trait. It feels like a lot of characters key personality traits are slowly morphing to that they just want to bang Sensei now. So every conversation just is “who we want to fuck” or “who I want to fuck” or “who they want to fuck” and it just never ends. Idk, I don’t think it was like this at the beginning of the game…

My favorite character is definitely Ami. I think her position as some sort of rogue factor in the world that the clean-up crew can’t even properly control is sick as hell. Didn’t really like her before but since she got her short hair, she’s been very fun to watch (and I think her design is way better). And there’s also a lot of unanswered questions with her character: why does she even like the MC that much? How much of her affection for the MC is tied with her mother? Cuz from recent chapters, it seems like she almost blames the MC for her mother’s death. Also if there’s no god inhabiting her, who is she constantly talking to?


I also like Niki a lot. It’s refreshing to have a character that genuinely wants the MC to be a better person. But I also really like her dynamic with Ami. Niki is one of the few characters that Ami treats differently – most likely because she occupies a role similar to Sekai. And there’s a few moments where Niki seemingly got past Ami’s façade and genuinely flustered her.


And given that Ami is beginning to fill the role as the “main antagonist,” I think this relationship will be examined more in the future. Especially since they’re not even subtle with this Niki vs Sekai dynamic.




But yeah, there's some other things I want to touch on but I'll probably look at some scenes again before I write anything up. Also, I kinda want to write an analysis on Ami. Is there any other context outside of the game on her character, since I know sometimes the writer includes extra info in places.
