spoilers.title: explanation
spoilers.html:
1. Nao-chan got her name from Kaori because of the kanji on her sweatshirt. When Kaori asked for her name, Nao-chan indicated she didn't have one. She also gave a small reaction when Kaori suggested the name, though that could be for any number of reasons.

2. The Xoanon said "You can call me a guardian angel if you like, but I prefer the name Nao". It doesn't explicitly state that Nao is its name, and the comparison suggests that "Nao" is in the same category as "guardian angel", i.e. a role rather than a given name.

3. The entity which possesses Tsuneyo in the white room and tries to get Sensei to plap plap her responds when Sensei addresses "Nao".
Some people suggested this is the Xoanon because it has the same eyes, but I think it has to be something different. The Xoanon doesn't interfere and there's zero commonality in their personalities.

It's hard for me to find any connection between these three, so even if I'm right, I don't know what it means to be "a Nao" (unless it really is just a synonym for guardian angel). It might be relevant that Nao-chan's kanji specifically means "honesty".

I appreciate your thoughts, but I'm sorry to say I disagree with most of your conclusions.
Click to expand...
1) “The duality between USER1 and USER2 is symbolic and almost entirely fictional. It's a status quo that Wires is maintaining on his own, because that's kind of his thing - keep the world running as it always has so he can maintain order. The problem is that USER1 is missing, and Wires is the only one running things at the start of the game. The HOPE in Chapter 1-2 is not a god and is working with Wires, not against him.”

This is an interesting theory, and I can certainly see how someone could come to that conclusion, but I’m really not sure how to reconcile the idea of USER1 being “missing” with him explicitly being in control of Terminal 23 in “Trinity Pt. III: Non Est Deus”, or him “having trouble connecting” during “Somnambula” (until he successfully manages to “log in” at the very end). Is the implication here that this is all just Tenchou secretly logging into his alt account and playing out the role of USER1 to intentionally perpetuate a make-belief conflict against himself? Why, though? What is the point of this charade? Like, the “maintain order” part makes sense, sure, but that alone doesn’t explain such a persistent need to keep up the illusion of USER1 being still alive. Who is USER2 trying to fool by doing this, when the only character who is even remotely aware of this “tug of war” between him and HOPE is Yasu? None of the other Wishing Well affiliated entities that we’ve seen thus far ever referenced this “cycle of succession” (to my knowledge) or even seemed to know who USER1 and USER 2 are, so why even bother with continuing to play pretend that there is a divine conflict going on?

Until this question gets sufficiently answered, I’m afraid that I cannot in full faith accept this interpretation as valid, I’m sorry.

2) “Himawari isn't the narrator of "Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)". I don't believe she narrated any events on that beach trip, but I'd have to double check.”

I mean, in “Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)” the narrator also says

“But every second spent here is like a forced vacation away from where you really want to be: my world, my house, where you’re seated at the table for a fancy dinner with your significant other, prepared and plated by an angel of your creation.”

which is *literally* a scene that happens later in this exact event chain (in “Bitter Cherries”, where Himawari prepares a romantic dinner for her mother and father), not to mention the narration itself ending with "Maybe I'll see you soon, I wonder?", so, like, I genuinely struggle to think who else could it be other than her. Plus, there is also the example from “A Matter of Time” that I mentioned in my “Colors/Moons” section, where the narrator directly mentions “settling down somewhere up north, maybe in Aomori” and clearly foreshadows Himawari pretending to be Maya in “Cities in Gifu”.

3) “Nodoka claims that Yasu believes this, but I'm fairly certain it isn't something Yasu ever actually said and certainly not something that she insists on.”

In “Horses or the Whispers of the Dead”, Yasu says that “there is no death – only a second plane of existence, much greater than this one”. Then in “Repentance” she reiterates that same claim, insisting that “there is a second plane of existence that lies directly on top of our current plane – it’s just impossible to see with your eyes only partially open”. Finally, in “Twisting Ivy” the girl says to Nodoka that “our world is not as simple as one above and one below” (“one above, one below” – two in total), and her following line about it actually being “an endless labyrinth of layers invisible to the naked eye” is said *in context* of it happening between the two planes (which is the explanation that is later referenced in “Fruits of Torment”).

Although, yes, you are admittedly correct in that Yasu *does* explicitly mention “multiple worlds on top of this one” in “More Human Than Human”, so I’m entirely willing to accept that I got at least some things wrong here.

1) “To be pedantic, the event starts on December 28 but the actual slumber party happens on December 30. Then during "Untitled" Long Maya says that it's December 28 again.”

Yes, I remember that point being discussed (the exact post is even saved in my screenshots folder, actually). This is exactly why I mentioned “the passage of time being effectively meaningless in Kumon-mi on both narrative and mechanical levels”, because those two additional days that clearly pass between the opening scene of “December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)” and the actual beginning of the slumber party might as well never have happened: as far as the story is concerned, it is *still* December 28th, regardless of what is written on the calendar. I wouldn’t even call it a gameplay oversight from Selebus as much as… the Wishing Well just fundamentally not giving a shit about how time actually works.

2) “Himawari's birthday (Dec 28) is only given on the wiki, not in the game itself.”

Ah, that explains it – thank you for clarifying this for me. I don’t really look at character profiles on the wiki, only the articles concerning specific events, so I never saw that.

3) “I think that's quite a stretch. I'm reasonably confident that the date of death is for Mr. Tojo, which I wrote about here. If you disagree with that post, I'm interested in hearing why.”

Huh, must have missed that post of yours somehow, because I genuinely do not remember reading that theory. I quite like it, actually: it makes a lot of sense and *definitely* fits much cleaner into the general picture than the version I proposed. So, no explicit disagreements from me.

4) “Maybe I missed it, but which world would Himawari have been born in? It couldn't be Sensei's world (Maya's wish) because the resets don't last long enough to carry a baby to term. In the previous world, he was in a monogamous relationship with Maya and showed no interest in Ayane, if we trust Ayane's own memories.”

The thing is, Himawari’s birth doesn’t really neatly fit into our known timeline *no matter how* you slice it – there are far too many pieces missing.

The only thing we currently have a direct confirmation of is that this specific broken iteration of Kumon-mi was explicitly created by Maya – who was, in turn, brought into existence by Akira as the result of his wish. What we *don’t* know for certain, however, is that the world Akira was in when he made that wish is indeed his “original” one, because one of Himawari’s lines in “Aomori” implies that he and Ayane share the same original world – and, well, it couldn't have been the “previous” one, since the version of Sensei who wished for Maya was seemingly never involved with Ayane, neither romantically nor sexually (although there were fantasies, since he frequently made Maya roleplay as her), so Himawari clearly doesn’t originate from there.

All of this leads me to assume that there is at least one more version of Kumon-mi – the one Hima was born and grew up in (and one we still know absolutely jack shit about, outside of some occasional vague references to it from a few events featuring Himawari as the narrator) – if not multiple other iterations of the city, and that Sensei (presumably due to his special ability to “slip”) was somehow repeatedly “transported” from one world to another, like what happened to him (and the others) during the fifth Halloween party, before eventually ending up here. That’s the only way how I can reconcile Hima’s claim that he is supposedly “the original” with everything else that we presently know about the greater timeline of events, without even mentioning how Akira’s implied suicide (that seemingly jumpstarts the entire narrative) or him being a younger brother to a divine entity (regardless of whether you believe that Nozomu is the OG HOPE or someone simply named after him) fit into this whole picture.

1) “Red=Sekai=USER3 and Green=Maya=USER2 are among the most well-established symbols in the game. It's been general consensus in this thread for as long as I've been here. So it's really weird that you don't acknowledge that and instead act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle.”

I “act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle” because, like I already mentioned in the section itself, there doesn’t appear to be a single consistent underlying logic to how the colors are used in this game, leading many (like Moonflare, for example, if I’m not mistaken) to a completely different consensus: that there *is* no logical way to properly attribute various colors to all of the different Gods, because Selebus simply does whatever he feels like without any actual regard to the previously established symbology or any form of thematic consistency. So this is still, for all intents and purposes, a mostly unexplored field of analysis which I decided to take a stab at, since at the end of the day my proposed (unproven) theory isn’t really any better or worse than all of the other (equally unproven) intepretations that were argued before me.

Furthermore, even if what you’re saying (about this being the general consensus in this thread) is indeed true, then it’s certainly not a consensus that *I* personally agree with, because while “Red=Sekai” and “Green=Maya” are 100% understandable observations to make, how they somehow translate to “Red=USER3” and “Green=USER2” is genuinely baffling to me. Outside of his (arguably, still not really explored) ties to Sekai, Pareidolia barely has *any* connection to the color red – far less than both HOPE and Tenchou, that’s for certain (which I extensively demonstrated in the corresponding section of my post) – and Wires being associated with the color green just because of that one single screen in “Infinity House” (plus maybe Maya mentioning him in "Baby Finches", and I guess also the color of leaves, because trees) is not really any more substantial or convincing than me connecting him to the color blue by virtue of Tenchou’s presumed relation to ocean.

The rest of your arguments, meanwhile, heavily rely on the aforementioned “USER2's actual enemy is USER3, while USER1 is missing” theory, the validity of which I already questioned earlier. They *might* be correct – I’m not denying them outright (and a few examples, like the logic behind Kaori’s red-green dichotomy, are certainly convincing, I’ll give you that) – but as long as we don’t have a much more explicit confirmation of HOPE being a fake God and the actual conflict occurring between Tenchou and Pareidolia instead, I’m not going to put too much trust in them, I’m sorry.

2) “What? I can't think of anything that's further from his goal. He wants to turn Sensei into a god/ubermensch who treats everyone else like tools, he doesn't want some kumbaya peaceful future.”

Does he? I mean, even ignoring the fact that a) he literally mentions “perfect harmony” in his final speech to Akira in “Friend”:

“and all I ask is that you wait to remember me. i ask that you wait until you’re lonely and create me once more. only then, can we find perfect harmony”

and b) we still to this day don’t actually know what Pareidolia’s true motives are, because he is a self-proclaimed liar who says one thing and does another, the “collector” thing could have easily been just a means to an end, not an end in itself. We already know that all three Gods “want the same thing, need the same thing”, and Pareidolia certainly wasn’t the only one pushing Akira in this direction – HOPE did it as well, and so does Ami at this present moment in the story – so who is to say that “transforming Sensei into an ubermensch” was the end point of his grand master plan, rather than a simple stepping stone towards something even greater?

Besides, I think you are being a bit narrow-minded in assuming “perfect harmony” to mean some idyllic utopia where everyone is constantly happy, or some other similarly generic interpretation of what the word “harmony” normally invokes. Remember, this is LiL, where nothing is ever what it seems and beauty always contains some strangeness in its proportions, so within that context Pareidolia’s “perfect harmony” could have just as easily been referring to some form of returning to the natural order of things, with Gods and humans living together as one (which *is* a concept that was brought up in the titular event, by the way). After all, nature itself is neither peaceful nor particularly kind, but it *is* harmonious, with all of its various components working in tandem each other to create something truly monumental and wonderous.

1) “I really wish you would use screenshots to give us context. If that isn't feasible for some reason, at least quote an excerpt from the script.”

This is a fair criticism. I, admittedly, don’t really like to use or rely on images all that much (especially because they are going to make my already gigantic posts even bigger) and *do* generally try to do my best to give provide all of the necessary context (by quoting certain lines in full, and so on), but the “Colors, Moons and the Trinity” section was already going on for way longer than I initially planned it to be, so I guess I kind of… skimped out on doing the full quote in that particular instance. Genuinely sorry for the inconvenience.

2) “I do want to give a piece of advice: present your idea before you talk about it. You start this section by saying you're arguing for a simple thesis, but you don't actually tell us what it is until the end of the second paragraph. That's really annoying to try to follow.”

I mean… I *want* to say that this is also a fair criticism, but also kind of… That first paragraph is fairly short, serving as a simple introduction to the segment, and the actual thesis itself is stated literally two sentences later. I suppose that the sentences *are* pretty big, so that might cause some issues with trying to follow along with my though, but still… it’s not like I waited multiple paragraphs to actually explain what I was talking about.

Dunno, maybe that’s just because I am extremely used to reading both books and essays with decently long-winded prose, so I don’t really have any issues retaining certain ideas from the opening parts until they are eventually revealed a few dozen/hundred words later, while someone who didn’t have as much exposure to the similar writing style could find themselves struggling to properly keep it all in their head. I’ll *try* to do better in the future, maybe, but I’m also not sure how much can I even change that aspect of how I write without just completely reinventing my comfortable and well-established approach to expressing myself through text.

Either way, thank you very much for writing such a detailed response! I similarly disagree with many of your counterarguments, but they were still a joy to read nonetheless.

None of the other Wishing Well affiliated entities that we’ve seen thus far ever referenced this “cycle of succession” (to my knowledge) or even seemed to know who USER1 and USER 2 are, so why even bother with continuing to play pretend that there is a divine conflict going on?
Until this question gets sufficiently answered, I’m afraid that I cannot in full faith accept this interpretation as valid, I’m sorry.
2) “Himawari isn't the narrator of "Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)". I don't believe she narrated any events on that beach trip, but I'd have to double check.”
I mean, in “Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)” the narrator also says
“But every second spent here is like a forced vacation away from where you really want to be: my world, my house, where you’re seated at the table for a fancy dinner with your significant other, prepared and plated by an angel of your creation.”
which is *literally* a scene that happens later in this exact event chain (in “Bitter Cherries”, where Himawari prepares a romantic dinner for her mother and father), not to mention the narration itself ending with "Maybe I'll see you soon, I wonder?", so, like, I genuinely struggle to think who else could it be other than her. Plus, there is also the example from “A Matter of Time” that I mentioned in my “Colors/Moons” section, where the narrator directly mentions “settling down somewhere up north, maybe in Aomori” and clearly foreshadows Himawari pretending to be Maya in “Cities in Gifu”.
3) “Nodoka claims that Yasu believes this, but I'm fairly certain it isn't something Yasu ever actually said and certainly not something that she insists on.”
In “Horses or the Whispers of the Dead”, Yasu says that “there is no death – only a second plane of existence, much greater than this one”. Then in “Repentance” she reiterates that same claim, insisting that “there is a second plane of existence that lies directly on top of our current plane – it’s just impossible to see with your eyes only partially open”. Finally, in “Twisting Ivy” the girl says to Nodoka that “our world is not as simple as one above and one below” (“one above, one below” – two in total), and her following line about it actually being “an endless labyrinth of layers invisible to the naked eye” is said *in context* of it happening between the two planes (which is the explanation that is later referenced in “Fruits of Torment”).
Although, yes, you are admittedly correct in that Yasu *does* explicitly mention “multiple worlds on top of this one” in “More Human Than Human”, so I’m entirely willing to accept that I got at least some things wrong here.

spoilers.title: Dates
spoilers.html:
1) “To be pedantic, the event starts on December 28 but the actual slumber party happens on December 30. Then during "Untitled" Long Maya says that it's December 28 again.”

Yes, I remember that point being discussed (the exact post is even saved in my screenshots folder, actually). This is exactly why I mentioned “the passage of time being effectively meaningless in Kumon-mi on both narrative and mechanical levels”, because those two additional days that clearly pass between the opening scene of “December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)” and the actual beginning of the slumber party might as well never have happened: as far as the story is concerned, it is *still* December 28th, regardless of what is written on the calendar. I wouldn’t even call it a gameplay oversight from Selebus as much as… the Wishing Well just fundamentally not giving a shit about how time actually works.

2) “Himawari's birthday (Dec 28) is only given on the wiki, not in the game itself.”

Ah, that explains it – thank you for clarifying this for me. I don’t really look at character profiles on the wiki, only the articles concerning specific events, so I never saw that.

3) “I think that's quite a stretch. I'm reasonably confident that the date of death is for Mr. Tojo, which I wrote about here. If you disagree with that post, I'm interested in hearing why.”

Huh, must have missed that post of yours somehow, because I genuinely do not remember reading that theory. I quite like it, actually: it makes a lot of sense and *definitely* fits much cleaner into the general picture than the version I proposed. So, no explicit disagreements from me.

4) “Maybe I missed it, but which world would Himawari have been born in? It couldn't be Sensei's world (Maya's wish) because the resets don't last long enough to carry a baby to term. In the previous world, he was in a monogamous relationship with Maya and showed no interest in Ayane, if we trust Ayane's own memories.”

The thing is, Himawari’s birth doesn’t really neatly fit into our known timeline *no matter how* you slice it – there are far too many pieces missing.

The only thing we currently have a direct confirmation of is that this specific broken iteration of Kumon-mi was explicitly created by Maya – who was, in turn, brought into existence by Akira as the result of his wish. What we *don’t* know for certain, however, is that the world Akira was in when he made that wish is indeed his “original” one, because one of Himawari’s lines in “Aomori” implies that he and Ayane share the same original world – and, well, it couldn't have been the “previous” one, since the version of Sensei who wished for Maya was seemingly never involved with Ayane, neither romantically nor sexually (although there were fantasies, since he frequently made Maya roleplay as her), so Himawari clearly doesn’t originate from there.

All of this leads me to assume that there is at least one more version of Kumon-mi – the one Hima was born and grew up in (and one we still know absolutely jack shit about, outside of some occasional vague references to it from a few events featuring Himawari as the narrator) – if not multiple other iterations of the city, and that Sensei (presumably due to his special ability to “slip”) was somehow repeatedly “transported” from one world to another, like what happened to him (and the others) during the fifth Halloween party, before eventually ending up here. That’s the only way how I can reconcile Hima’s claim that he is supposedly “the original” with everything else that we presently know about the greater timeline of events, without even mentioning how Akira’s implied suicide (that seemingly jumpstarts the entire narrative) or him being a younger brother to a divine entity (regardless of whether you believe that Nozomu is the OG HOPE or someone simply named after him) fit into this whole picture.

spoilers.title: Colors
spoilers.html:
1) “Red=Sekai=USER3 and Green=Maya=USER2 are among the most well-established symbols in the game. It's been general consensus in this thread for as long as I've been here. So it's really weird that you don't acknowledge that and instead act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle.”

I “act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle” because, like I already mentioned in the section itself, there doesn’t appear to be a single consistent underlying logic to how the colors are used in this game, leading many (like Moonflare, for example, if I’m not mistaken) to a completely different consensus: that there *is* no logical way to properly attribute various colors to all of the different Gods, because Selebus simply does whatever he feels like without any actual regard to the previously established symbology or any form of thematic consistency. So this is still, for all intents and purposes, a mostly unexplored field of analysis which I decided to take a stab at, since at the end of the day my proposed (unproven) theory isn’t really any better or worse than all of the other (equally unproven) intepretations that were argued before me.

Furthermore, even if what you’re saying (about this being the general consensus in this thread) is indeed true, then it’s certainly not a consensus that *I* personally agree with, because while “Red=Sekai” and “Green=Maya” are 100% understandable observations to make, how they somehow translate to “Red=USER3” and “Green=USER2” is genuinely baffling to me. Outside of his (arguably, still not really explored) ties to Sekai, Pareidolia barely has *any* connection to the color red – far less than both HOPE and Tenchou, that’s for certain (which I extensively demonstrated in the corresponding section of my post) – and Wires being associated with the color green just because of that one single screen in “Infinity House” (plus maybe Maya mentioning him in "Baby Finches", and I guess also the color of leaves, because trees) is not really any more substantial or convincing than me connecting him to the color blue by virtue of Tenchou’s presumed relation to ocean.

The rest of your arguments, meanwhile, heavily rely on the aforementioned “USER2's actual enemy is USER3, while USER1 is missing” theory, the validity of which I already questioned earlier. They *might* be correct – I’m not denying them outright (and a few examples, like the logic behind Kaori’s red-green dichotomy, are certainly convincing, I’ll give you that) – but as long as we don’t have a much more explicit confirmation of HOPE being a fake God and the actual conflict occurring between Tenchou and Pareidolia instead, I’m not going to put too much trust in them, I’m sorry.

2) “What? I can't think of anything that's further from his goal. He wants to turn Sensei into a god/ubermensch who treats everyone else like tools, he doesn't want some kumbaya peaceful future.”

Does he? I mean, even ignoring the fact that a) he literally mentions “perfect harmony” in his final speech to Akira in “Friend”:

“and all I ask is that you wait to remember me. i ask that you wait until you’re lonely and create me once more. only then, can we find perfect harmony”

and b) we still to this day don’t actually know what Pareidolia’s true motives are, because he is a self-proclaimed liar who says one thing and does another, the “collector” thing could have easily been just a means to an end, not an end in itself. We already know that all three Gods “want the same thing, need the same thing”, and Pareidolia certainly wasn’t the only one pushing Akira in this direction – HOPE did it as well, and so does Ami at this present moment in the story – so who is to say that “transforming Sensei into an ubermensch” was the end point of his grand master plan, rather than a simple stepping stone towards something even greater?

Besides, I think you are being a bit narrow-minded in assuming “perfect harmony” to mean some idyllic utopia where everyone is constantly happy, or some other similarly generic interpretation of what the word “harmony” normally invokes. Remember, this is LiL, where nothing is ever what it seems and beauty always contains some strangeness in its proportions, so within that context Pareidolia’s “perfect harmony” could have just as easily been referring to some form of returning to the natural order of things, with Gods and humans living together as one (which *is* a concept that was brought up in the titular event, by the way). After all, nature itself is neither peaceful nor particularly kind, but it *is* harmonious, with all of its various components working in tandem each other to create something truly monumental and wonderous.

spoilers.title: Some additional comments in relation to my presentation/writing style
spoilers.html:
1) “I really wish you would use screenshots to give us context. If that isn't feasible for some reason, at least quote an excerpt from the script.”

This is a fair criticism. I, admittedly, don’t really like to use or rely on images all that much (especially because they are going to make my already gigantic posts even bigger) and *do* generally try to do my best to give provide all of the necessary context (by quoting certain lines in full, and so on), but the “Colors, Moons and the Trinity” section was already going on for way longer than I initially planned it to be, so I guess I kind of… skimped out on doing the full quote in that particular instance. Genuinely sorry for the inconvenience.

2) “I do want to give a piece of advice: present your idea before you talk about it. You start this section by saying you're arguing for a simple thesis, but you don't actually tell us what it is until the end of the second paragraph. That's really annoying to try to follow.”

I mean… I *want* to say that this is also a fair criticism, but also kind of… That first paragraph is fairly short, serving as a simple introduction to the segment, and the actual thesis itself is stated literally two sentences later. I suppose that the sentences *are* pretty big, so that might cause some issues with trying to follow along with my though, but still… it’s not like I waited multiple paragraphs to actually explain what I was talking about.

Dunno, maybe that’s just because I am extremely used to reading both books and essays with decently long-winded prose, so I don’t really have any issues retaining certain ideas from the opening parts until they are eventually revealed a few dozen/hundred words later, while someone who didn’t have as much exposure to the similar writing style could find themselves struggling to properly keep it all in their head. I’ll *try* to do better in the future, maybe, but I’m also not sure how much can I even change that aspect of how I write without just completely reinventing my comfortable and well-established approach to expressing myself through text.

I stumbled on this game through a twitter post last year, downloaded it out of curiosity on the hopes that it was some crazed, depraved, psychological thriller, and was not disappointed. But I went thru this game without knowing of any dedicated threads or YouTube videos or really anything with other people’s thoughts on this game, and I really didn’t and haven’t bothered to join the discord, especially while going thru the game as to avoid spoilers and also because of what I’ve heard about the author while going thru this thread. So I’m glad to say it’s been great to find this site, and to read the various posts and all the theories and whatnot. Lots to add to my overall thoughts on the game. That being said I do have some questions…. Sorry in advance if they’ve already been answered somewhere else here already

who is the “final boss” that is to say, the main antagonist of LiL? Is it HOPE? Nozomu? Pariedolia? Sekai?! Ami?or has it not even really been revealed or hinted at yet? This may sound broad but I am interested in hearing thoughts on this. I mean I feel like I’m missing something here I dunno.

do we have a comprehensive list of all known narrators thus far? I know Himawari is one of them. I know Ami is one them. I know Pareidolia is technically one of them too. But I feel like there are several more that I can’t figure out. I know also it’s not really the main point to figure this out, and Selebus has gone on to say that even he himself could be a narrator, but still I’m just curious. Also, I think Maya might be a narrator as well. But I don’t have my pc nearby at the moment, so I can’t grab certain examples that have led me to believe this, sorry.

just what exactly are they? Why specifically are they variants of Maya? I understand Maya herself isn’t even real, but still… it gnaws at me. Especially Amiokay. Just what is her purpose? I mean what is she exactly? Amiokay is probably the most interesting Maya variant out of the 4 we know so far. Does she work for one of these entities like Long Maya and Moyo? Or is she an older version of our Maya that we all know and love? What is her ties to the TSS’s? Why is her name “Amiokay” in the first place? posts.content_html_raw:
CharlotteWiltshire26 said:
1) “The duality between USER1 and USER2 is symbolic and almost entirely fictional. It's a status quo that Wires is maintaining on his own, because that's kind of his thing - keep the world running as it always has so he can maintain order. The problem is that USER1 is missing, and Wires is the only one running things at the start of the game. The HOPE in Chapter 1-2 is not a god and is working with Wires, not against him.”

This is an interesting theory, and I can certainly see how someone could come to that conclusion, but I’m really not sure how to reconcile the idea of USER1 being “missing” with him explicitly being in control of Terminal 23 in “Trinity Pt. III: Non Est Deus”, or him “having trouble connecting” during “Somnambula” (until he successfully manages to “log in” at the very end). Is the implication here that this is all just Tenchou secretly logging into his alt account and playing out the role of USER1 to intentionally perpetuate a make-belief conflict against himself? Why, though? What is the point of this charade? Like, the “maintain order” part makes sense, sure, but that alone doesn’t explain such a persistent need to keep up the illusion of USER1 being still alive. Who is USER2 trying to fool by doing this, when the only character who is even remotely aware of this “tug of war” between him and HOPE is Yasu? None of the other Wishing Well affiliated entities that we’ve seen thus far ever referenced this “cycle of succession” (to my knowledge) or even seemed to know who USER1 and USER 2 are, so why even bother with continuing to play pretend that there is a divine conflict going on?

Until this question gets sufficiently answered, I’m afraid that I cannot in full faith accept this interpretation as valid, I’m sorry.

2) “Himawari isn't the narrator of "Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)". I don't believe she narrated any events on that beach trip, but I'd have to double check.”

I mean, in “Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)” the narrator also says

“But every second spent here is like a forced vacation away from where you really want to be: my world, my house, where you’re seated at the table for a fancy dinner with your significant other, prepared and plated by an angel of your creation.”

which is *literally* a scene that happens later in this exact event chain (in “Bitter Cherries”, where Himawari prepares a romantic dinner for her mother and father), not to mention the narration itself ending with "Maybe I'll see you soon, I wonder?", so, like, I genuinely struggle to think who else could it be other than her. Plus, there is also the example from “A Matter of Time” that I mentioned in my “Colors/Moons” section, where the narrator directly mentions “settling down somewhere up north, maybe in Aomori” and clearly foreshadows Himawari pretending to be Maya in “Cities in Gifu”.

3) “Nodoka claims that Yasu believes this, but I'm fairly certain it isn't something Yasu ever actually said and certainly not something that she insists on.”

In “Horses or the Whispers of the Dead”, Yasu says that “there is no death – only a second plane of existence, much greater than this one”. Then in “Repentance” she reiterates that same claim, insisting that “there is a second plane of existence that lies directly on top of our current plane – it’s just impossible to see with your eyes only partially open”. Finally, in “Twisting Ivy” the girl says to Nodoka that “our world is not as simple as one above and one below” (“one above, one below” – two in total), and her following line about it actually being “an endless labyrinth of layers invisible to the naked eye” is said *in context* of it happening between the two planes (which is the explanation that is later referenced in “Fruits of Torment”).

Although, yes, you are admittedly correct in that Yasu *does* explicitly mention “multiple worlds on top of this one” in “More Human Than Human”, so I’m entirely willing to accept that I got at least some things wrong here.

1) “To be pedantic, the event starts on December 28 but the actual slumber party happens on December 30. Then during "Untitled" Long Maya says that it's December 28 again.”

Yes, I remember that point being discussed (the exact post is even saved in my screenshots folder, actually). This is exactly why I mentioned “the passage of time being effectively meaningless in Kumon-mi on both narrative and mechanical levels”, because those two additional days that clearly pass between the opening scene of “December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)” and the actual beginning of the slumber party might as well never have happened: as far as the story is concerned, it is *still* December 28th, regardless of what is written on the calendar. I wouldn’t even call it a gameplay oversight from Selebus as much as… the Wishing Well just fundamentally not giving a shit about how time actually works.

2) “Himawari's birthday (Dec 28) is only given on the wiki, not in the game itself.”

Ah, that explains it – thank you for clarifying this for me. I don’t really look at character profiles on the wiki, only the articles concerning specific events, so I never saw that.

3) “I think that's quite a stretch. I'm reasonably confident that the date of death is for Mr. Tojo, which I wrote about here. If you disagree with that post, I'm interested in hearing why.”

Huh, must have missed that post of yours somehow, because I genuinely do not remember reading that theory. I quite like it, actually: it makes a lot of sense and *definitely* fits much cleaner into the general picture than the version I proposed. So, no explicit disagreements from me.

4) “Maybe I missed it, but which world would Himawari have been born in? It couldn't be Sensei's world (Maya's wish) because the resets don't last long enough to carry a baby to term. In the previous world, he was in a monogamous relationship with Maya and showed no interest in Ayane, if we trust Ayane's own memories.”

The thing is, Himawari’s birth doesn’t really neatly fit into our known timeline *no matter how* you slice it – there are far too many pieces missing.

The only thing we currently have a direct confirmation of is that this specific broken iteration of Kumon-mi was explicitly created by Maya – who was, in turn, brought into existence by Akira as the result of his wish. What we *don’t* know for certain, however, is that the world Akira was in when he made that wish is indeed his “original” one, because one of Himawari’s lines in “Aomori” implies that he and Ayane share the same original world – and, well, it couldn't have been the “previous” one, since the version of Sensei who wished for Maya was seemingly never involved with Ayane, neither romantically nor sexually (although there were fantasies, since he frequently made Maya roleplay as her), so Himawari clearly doesn’t originate from there.

All of this leads me to assume that there is at least one more version of Kumon-mi – the one Hima was born and grew up in (and one we still know absolutely jack shit about, outside of some occasional vague references to it from a few events featuring Himawari as the narrator) – if not multiple other iterations of the city, and that Sensei (presumably due to his special ability to “slip”) was somehow repeatedly “transported” from one world to another, like what happened to him (and the others) during the fifth Halloween party, before eventually ending up here. That’s the only way how I can reconcile Hima’s claim that he is supposedly “the original” with everything else that we presently know about the greater timeline of events, without even mentioning how Akira’s implied suicide (that seemingly jumpstarts the entire narrative) or him being a younger brother to a divine entity (regardless of whether you believe that Nozomu is the OG HOPE or someone simply named after him) fit into this whole picture.

1) “Red=Sekai=USER3 and Green=Maya=USER2 are among the most well-established symbols in the game. It's been general consensus in this thread for as long as I've been here. So it's really weird that you don't acknowledge that and instead act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle.”

I “act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle” because, like I already mentioned in the section itself, there doesn’t appear to be a single consistent underlying logic to how the colors are used in this game, leading many (like Moonflare, for example, if I’m not mistaken) to a completely different consensus: that there *is* no logical way to properly attribute various colors to all of the different Gods, because Selebus simply does whatever he feels like without any actual regard to the previously established symbology or any form of thematic consistency. So this is still, for all intents and purposes, a mostly unexplored field of analysis which I decided to take a stab at, since at the end of the day my proposed (unproven) theory isn’t really any better or worse than all of the other (equally unproven) intepretations that were argued before me.

Furthermore, even if what you’re saying (about this being the general consensus in this thread) is indeed true, then it’s certainly not a consensus that *I* personally agree with, because while “Red=Sekai” and “Green=Maya” are 100% understandable observations to make, how they somehow translate to “Red=USER3” and “Green=USER2” is genuinely baffling to me. Outside of his (arguably, still not really explored) ties to Sekai, Pareidolia barely has *any* connection to the color red – far less than both HOPE and Tenchou, that’s for certain (which I extensively demonstrated in the corresponding section of my post) – and Wires being associated with the color green just because of that one single screen in “Infinity House” (plus maybe Maya mentioning him in "Baby Finches", and I guess also the color of leaves, because trees) is not really any more substantial or convincing than me connecting him to the color blue by virtue of Tenchou’s presumed relation to ocean.

The rest of your arguments, meanwhile, heavily rely on the aforementioned “USER2's actual enemy is USER3, while USER1 is missing” theory, the validity of which I already questioned earlier. They *might* be correct – I’m not denying them outright (and a few examples, like the logic behind Kaori’s red-green dichotomy, are certainly convincing, I’ll give you that) – but as long as we don’t have a much more explicit confirmation of HOPE being a fake God and the actual conflict occurring between Tenchou and Pareidolia instead, I’m not going to put too much trust in them, I’m sorry.

2) “What? I can't think of anything that's further from his goal. He wants to turn Sensei into a god/ubermensch who treats everyone else like tools, he doesn't want some kumbaya peaceful future.”

Does he? I mean, even ignoring the fact that a) he literally mentions “perfect harmony” in his final speech to Akira in “Friend”:

“and all I ask is that you wait to remember me. i ask that you wait until you’re lonely and create me once more. only then, can we find perfect harmony”

and b) we still to this day don’t actually know what Pareidolia’s true motives are, because he is a self-proclaimed liar who says one thing and does another, the “collector” thing could have easily been just a means to an end, not an end in itself. We already know that all three Gods “want the same thing, need the same thing”, and Pareidolia certainly wasn’t the only one pushing Akira in this direction – HOPE did it as well, and so does Ami at this present moment in the story – so who is to say that “transforming Sensei into an ubermensch” was the end point of his grand master plan, rather than a simple stepping stone towards something even greater?

Besides, I think you are being a bit narrow-minded in assuming “perfect harmony” to mean some idyllic utopia where everyone is constantly happy, or some other similarly generic interpretation of what the word “harmony” normally invokes. Remember, this is LiL, where nothing is ever what it seems and beauty always contains some strangeness in its proportions, so within that context Pareidolia’s “perfect harmony” could have just as easily been referring to some form of returning to the natural order of things, with Gods and humans living together as one (which *is* a concept that was brought up in the titular event, by the way). After all, nature itself is neither peaceful nor particularly kind, but it *is* harmonious, with all of its various components working in tandem each other to create something truly monumental and wonderous.

1) “I really wish you would use screenshots to give us context. If that isn't feasible for some reason, at least quote an excerpt from the script.”

This is a fair criticism. I, admittedly, don’t really like to use or rely on images all that much (especially because they are going to make my already gigantic posts even bigger) and *do* generally try to do my best to give provide all of the necessary context (by quoting certain lines in full, and so on), but the “Colors, Moons and the Trinity” section was already going on for way longer than I initially planned it to be, so I guess I kind of… skimped out on doing the full quote in that particular instance. Genuinely sorry for the inconvenience.

2) “I do want to give a piece of advice: present your idea before you talk about it. You start this section by saying you're arguing for a simple thesis, but you don't actually tell us what it is until the end of the second paragraph. That's really annoying to try to follow.”

I mean… I *want* to say that this is also a fair criticism, but also kind of… That first paragraph is fairly short, serving as a simple introduction to the segment, and the actual thesis itself is stated literally two sentences later. I suppose that the sentences *are* pretty big, so that might cause some issues with trying to follow along with my though, but still… it’s not like I waited multiple paragraphs to actually explain what I was talking about.

Dunno, maybe that’s just because I am extremely used to reading both books and essays with decently long-winded prose, so I don’t really have any issues retaining certain ideas from the opening parts until they are eventually revealed a few dozen/hundred words later, while someone who didn’t have as much exposure to the similar writing style could find themselves struggling to properly keep it all in their head. I’ll *try* to do better in the future, maybe, but I’m also not sure how much can I even change that aspect of how I write without just completely reinventing my comfortable and well-established approach to expressing myself through text.

Either way, thank you very much for writing such a detailed response! I similarly disagree with many of your counterarguments, but they were still a joy to read nonetheless.

Spoiler:
HOPE and Wires
1) “The duality between USER1 and USER2 is symbolic and almost entirely fictional. It's a status quo that Wires is maintaining on his own, because that's kind of his thing - keep the world running as it always has so he can maintain order. The problem is that USER1 is missing, and Wires is the only one running things at the start of the game. The HOPE in Chapter 1-2 is not a god and is working with Wires, not against him.”
This is an interesting theory, and I can certainly see how someone could come to that conclusion, but I’m really not sure how to reconcile the idea of USER1 being “missing” with him explicitly being in control of Terminal 23 in “Trinity Pt. III: Non Est Deus”, or him “having trouble connecting” during “Somnambula” (until he successfully manages to “log in” at the very end). Is the implication here that this is all just Tenchou secretly logging into his alt account and playing out the role of USER1 to intentionally perpetuate a make-belief conflict against himself? Why, though? What is the point of this charade? Like, the “maintain order” part makes sense, sure, but that alone doesn’t explain such a persistent need to keep up the illusion of USER1 being still alive. Who is USER2 trying to fool by doing this, when the only character who is even remotely aware of this “tug of war” between him and HOPE is Yasu? None of the other Wishing Well affiliated entities that we’ve seen thus far ever referenced this “cycle of succession” (to my knowledge) or even seemed to know who USER1 and USER 2 are, so why even bother with continuing to play pretend that there is a divine conflict going on?
Until this question gets sufficiently answered, I’m afraid that I cannot in full faith accept this interpretation as valid, I’m sorry.
2) “Himawari isn't the narrator of "Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)". I don't believe she narrated any events on that beach trip, but I'd have to double check.”
I mean, in “Legacy of Thaum (On a Bus)” the narrator also says
“But every second spent here is like a forced vacation away from where you really want to be: my world, my house, where you’re seated at the table for a fancy dinner with your significant other, prepared and plated by an angel of your creation.”
which is *literally* a scene that happens later in this exact event chain (in “Bitter Cherries”, where Himawari prepares a romantic dinner for her mother and father), not to mention the narration itself ending with "Maybe I'll see you soon, I wonder?", so, like, I genuinely struggle to think who else could it be other than her. Plus, there is also the example from “A Matter of Time” that I mentioned in my “Colors/Moons” section, where the narrator directly mentions “settling down somewhere up north, maybe in Aomori” and clearly foreshadows Himawari pretending to be Maya in “Cities in Gifu”.
3) “Nodoka claims that Yasu believes this, but I'm fairly certain it isn't something Yasu ever actually said and certainly not something that she insists on.”
In “Horses or the Whispers of the Dead”, Yasu says that “there is no death – only a second plane of existence, much greater than this one”. Then in “Repentance” she reiterates that same claim, insisting that “there is a second plane of existence that lies directly on top of our current plane – it’s just impossible to see with your eyes only partially open”. Finally, in “Twisting Ivy” the girl says to Nodoka that “our world is not as simple as one above and one below” (“one above, one below” – two in total), and her following line about it actually being “an endless labyrinth of layers invisible to the naked eye” is said *in context* of it happening between the two planes (which is the explanation that is later referenced in “Fruits of Torment”).
Although, yes, you are admittedly correct in that Yasu *does* explicitly mention “multiple worlds on top of this one” in “More Human Than Human”, so I’m entirely willing to accept that I got at least some things wrong here.
Spoiler:
Dates
1) “To be pedantic, the event starts on December 28 but the actual slumber party happens on December 30. Then during "Untitled" Long Maya says that it's December 28 again.”
Yes, I remember that point being discussed (the exact post is even saved in my screenshots folder, actually). This is exactly why I mentioned “the passage of time being effectively meaningless in Kumon-mi on both narrative and mechanical levels”, because those two additional days that clearly pass between the opening scene of “December 28, 2020 (Clay & Clockwork)” and the actual beginning of the slumber party might as well never have happened: as far as the story is concerned, it is *still* December 28th, regardless of what is written on the calendar. I wouldn’t even call it a gameplay oversight from Selebus as much as… the Wishing Well just fundamentally not giving a shit about how time actually works.
2) “Himawari's birthday (Dec 28) is only given on the wiki, not in the game itself.”
Ah, that explains it – thank you for clarifying this for me. I don’t really look at character profiles on the wiki, only the articles concerning specific events, so I never saw that.
3) “I think that's quite a stretch. I'm reasonably confident that the date of death is for Mr. Tojo, which I wrote about here. If you disagree with that post, I'm interested in hearing why.”
Huh, must have missed that post of yours somehow, because I genuinely do not remember reading that theory. I quite like it, actually: it makes a lot of sense and *definitely* fits much cleaner into the general picture than the version I proposed. So, no explicit disagreements from me.
4) “Maybe I missed it, but which world would Himawari have been born in? It couldn't be Sensei's world (Maya's wish) because the resets don't last long enough to carry a baby to term. In the previous world, he was in a monogamous relationship with Maya and showed no interest in Ayane, if we trust Ayane's own memories.”
The thing is, Himawari’s birth doesn’t really neatly fit into our known timeline *no matter how* you slice it – there are far too many pieces missing.
The only thing we currently have a direct confirmation of is that this specific broken iteration of Kumon-mi was explicitly created by Maya – who was, in turn, brought into existence by Akira as the result of his wish. What we *don’t* know for certain, however, is that the world Akira was in when he made that wish is indeed his “original” one, because one of Himawari’s lines in “Aomori” implies that he and Ayane share the same original world – and, well, it couldn't have been the “previous” one, since the version of Sensei who wished for Maya was seemingly never involved with Ayane, neither romantically nor sexually (although there were fantasies, since he frequently made Maya roleplay as her), so Himawari clearly doesn’t originate from there.
All of this leads me to assume that there is at least one more version of Kumon-mi – the one Hima was born and grew up in (and one we still know absolutely jack shit about, outside of some occasional vague references to it from a few events featuring Himawari as the narrator) – if not multiple other iterations of the city, and that Sensei (presumably due to his special ability to “slip”) was somehow repeatedly “transported” from one world to another, like what happened to him (and the others) during the fifth Halloween party, before eventually ending up here. That’s the only way how I can reconcile Hima’s claim that he is supposedly “the original” with everything else that we presently know about the greater timeline of events, without even mentioning how Akira’s implied suicide (that seemingly jumpstarts the entire narrative) or him being a younger brother to a divine entity (regardless of whether you believe that Nozomu is the OG HOPE or someone simply named after him) fit into this whole picture.
Spoiler:
Colors
1) “Red=Sekai=USER3 and Green=Maya=USER2 are among the most well-established symbols in the game. It's been general consensus in this thread for as long as I've been here. So it's really weird that you don't acknowledge that and instead act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle.”
I “act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle” because, like I already mentioned in the section itself, there doesn’t appear to be a single consistent underlying logic to how the colors are used in this game, leading many (like Moonflare, for example, if I’m not mistaken) to a completely different consensus: that there *is* no logical way to properly attribute various colors to all of the different Gods, because Selebus simply does whatever he feels like without any actual regard to the previously established symbology or any form of thematic consistency. So this is still, for all intents and purposes, a mostly unexplored field of analysis which I decided to take a stab at, since at the end of the day my proposed (unproven) theory isn’t really any better or worse than all of the other (equally unproven) intepretations that were argued before me.
Furthermore, even if what you’re saying (about this being the general consensus in this thread) is indeed true, then it’s certainly not a consensus that *I* personally agree with, because while “Red=Sekai” and “Green=Maya” are 100% understandable observations to make, how they somehow translate to “Red=USER3” and “Green=USER2” is genuinely baffling to me. Outside of his (arguably, still not really explored) ties to Sekai, Pareidolia barely has *any* connection to the color red – far less than both HOPE and Tenchou, that’s for certain (which I extensively demonstrated in the corresponding section of my post) – and Wires being associated with the color green just because of that one single screen in “Infinity House” (plus maybe Maya mentioning him in "Baby Finches", and I guess also the color of leaves, because trees) is not really any more substantial or convincing than me connecting him to the color blue by virtue of Tenchou’s presumed relation to ocean.
The rest of your arguments, meanwhile, heavily rely on the aforementioned “USER2's actual enemy is USER3, while USER1 is missing” theory, the validity of which I already questioned earlier. They *might* be correct – I’m not denying them outright (and a few examples, like the logic behind Kaori’s red-green dichotomy, are certainly convincing, I’ll give you that) – but as long as we don’t have a much more explicit confirmation of HOPE being a fake God and the actual conflict occurring between Tenchou and Pareidolia instead, I’m not going to put too much trust in them, I’m sorry.
2) “What? I can't think of anything that's further from his goal. He wants to turn Sensei into a god/ubermensch who treats everyone else like tools, he doesn't want some kumbaya peaceful future.”
Does he? I mean, even ignoring the fact that a) he literally mentions “perfect harmony” in his final speech to Akira in “Friend”:
“and all I ask is that you wait to remember me. i ask that you wait until you’re lonely and create me once more. only then, can we find perfect harmony”
and b) we still to this day don’t actually know what Pareidolia’s true motives are, because he is a self-proclaimed liar who says one thing and does another, the “collector” thing could have easily been just a means to an end, not an end in itself. We already know that all three Gods “want the same thing, need the same thing”, and Pareidolia certainly wasn’t the only one pushing Akira in this direction – HOPE did it as well, and so does Ami at this present moment in the story – so who is to say that “transforming Sensei into an ubermensch” was the end point of his grand master plan, rather than a simple stepping stone towards something even greater?
Besides, I think you are being a bit narrow-minded in assuming “perfect harmony” to mean some idyllic utopia where everyone is constantly happy, or some other similarly generic interpretation of what the word “harmony” normally invokes. Remember, this is LiL, where nothing is ever what it seems and beauty always contains some strangeness in its proportions, so within that context Pareidolia’s “perfect harmony” could have just as easily been referring to some form of returning to the natural order of things, with Gods and humans living together as one (which *is* a concept that was brought up in the titular event, by the way). After all, nature itself is neither peaceful nor particularly kind, but it *is* harmonious, with all of its various components working in tandem each other to create something truly monumental and wonderous.
Spoiler:
Some additional comments in relation to my presentation/writing style
1) “I really wish you would use screenshots to give us context. If that isn't feasible for some reason, at least quote an excerpt from the script.”
This is a fair criticism. I, admittedly, don’t really like to use or rely on images all that much (especially because they are going to make my already gigantic posts even bigger) and *do* generally try to do my best to give provide all of the necessary context (by quoting certain lines in full, and so on), but the “Colors, Moons and the Trinity” section was already going on for way longer than I initially planned it to be, so I guess I kind of… skimped out on doing the full quote in that particular instance. Genuinely sorry for the inconvenience.
2) “I do want to give a piece of advice: present your idea before you talk about it. You start this section by saying you're arguing for a simple thesis, but you don't actually tell us what it is until the end of the second paragraph. That's really annoying to try to follow.”
I mean… I *want* to say that this is also a fair criticism, but also kind of… That first paragraph is fairly short, serving as a simple introduction to the segment, and the actual thesis itself is stated literally two sentences later. I suppose that the sentences *are* pretty big, so that might cause some issues with trying to follow along with my though, but still… it’s not like I waited multiple paragraphs to actually explain what I was talking about.
Dunno, maybe that’s just because I am extremely used to reading both books and essays with decently long-winded prose, so I don’t really have any issues retaining certain ideas from the opening parts until they are eventually revealed a few dozen/hundred words later, while someone who didn’t have as much exposure to the similar writing style could find themselves struggling to properly keep it all in their head. I’ll *try* to do better in the future, maybe, but I’m also not sure how much can I even change that aspect of how I write without just completely reinventing my comfortable and well-established approach to expressing myself through text.
Either way, thank you very much for writing such a detailed response! I similarly disagree with many of your counterarguments, but they were still a joy to read nonetheless.

spoilers.title: Colors
spoilers.html:
1) “Red=Sekai=USER3 and Green=Maya=USER2 are among the most well-established symbols in the game. It's been general consensus in this thread for as long as I've been here. So it's really weird that you don't acknowledge that and instead act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle.”

I “act like the colors are a previously unexplored puzzle” because, like I already mentioned in the section itself, there doesn’t appear to be a single consistent underlying logic to how the colors are used in this game, leading many (like Moonflare, for example, if I’m not mistaken) to a completely different consensus: that there *is* no logical way to properly attribute various colors to all of the different Gods, because Selebus simply does whatever he feels like without any actual regard to the previously established symbology or any form of thematic consistency. So this is still, for all intents and purposes, a mostly unexplored field of analysis which I decided to take a stab at, since at the end of the day my proposed (unproven) theory isn’t really any better or worse than all of the other (equally unproven) intepretations that were argued before me.

Furthermore, even if what you’re saying (about this being the general consensus in this thread) is indeed true, then it’s certainly not a consensus that *I* personally agree with, because while “Red=Sekai” and “Green=Maya” are 100% understandable observations to make, how they somehow translate to “Red=USER3” and “Green=USER2” is genuinely baffling to me. Outside of his (arguably, still not really explored) ties to Sekai, Pareidolia barely has *any* connection to the color red – far less than both HOPE and Tenchou, that’s for certain (which I extensively demonstrated in the corresponding section of my post) – and Wires being associated with the color green just because of that one single screen in “Infinity House” (plus maybe Maya mentioning him in "Baby Finches", and I guess also the color of leaves, because trees) is not really any more substantial or convincing than me connecting him to the color blue by virtue of Tenchou’s presumed relation to ocean.

The rest of your arguments, meanwhile, heavily rely on the aforementioned “USER2's actual enemy is USER3, while USER1 is missing” theory, the validity of which I already questioned earlier. They *might* be correct – I’m not denying them outright (and a few examples, like the logic behind Kaori’s red-green dichotomy, are certainly convincing, I’ll give you that) – but as long as we don’t have a much more explicit confirmation of HOPE being a fake God and the actual conflict occurring between Tenchou and Pareidolia instead, I’m not going to put too much trust in them, I’m sorry.

2) “What? I can't think of anything that's further from his goal. He wants to turn Sensei into a god/ubermensch who treats everyone else like tools, he doesn't want some kumbaya peaceful future.”

Does he? I mean, even ignoring the fact that a) he literally mentions “perfect harmony” in his final speech to Akira in “Friend”:

“and all I ask is that you wait to remember me. i ask that you wait until you’re lonely and create me once more. only then, can we find perfect harmony”

and b) we still to this day don’t actually know what Pareidolia’s true motives are, because he is a self-proclaimed liar who says one thing and does another, the “collector” thing could have easily been just a means to an end, not an end in itself. We already know that all three Gods “want the same thing, need the same thing”, and Pareidolia certainly wasn’t the only one pushing Akira in this direction – HOPE did it as well, and so does Ami at this present moment in the story – so who is to say that “transforming Sensei into an ubermensch” was the end point of his grand master plan, rather than a simple stepping stone towards something even greater?

Besides, I think you are being a bit narrow-minded in assuming “perfect harmony” to mean some idyllic utopia where everyone is constantly happy, or some other similarly generic interpretation of what the word “harmony” normally invokes. Remember, this is LiL, where nothing is ever what it seems and beauty always contains some strangeness in its proportions, so within that context Pareidolia’s “perfect harmony” could have just as easily been referring to some form of returning to the natural order of things, with Gods and humans living together as one (which *is* a concept that was brought up in the titular event, by the way). After all, nature itself is neither peaceful nor particularly kind, but it *is* harmonious, with all of its various components working in tandem each other to create something truly monumental and wonderous.

spoilers.title: Some additional comments in relation to my presentation/writing style
spoilers.html:
1) “I really wish you would use screenshots to give us context. If that isn't feasible for some reason, at least quote an excerpt from the script.”

This is a fair criticism. I, admittedly, don’t really like to use or rely on images all that much (especially because they are going to make my already gigantic posts even bigger) and *do* generally try to do my best to give provide all of the necessary context (by quoting certain lines in full, and so on), but the “Colors, Moons and the Trinity” section was already going on for way longer than I initially planned it to be, so I guess I kind of… skimped out on doing the full quote in that particular instance. Genuinely sorry for the inconvenience.

2) “I do want to give a piece of advice: present your idea before you talk about it. You start this section by saying you're arguing for a simple thesis, but you don't actually tell us what it is until the end of the second paragraph. That's really annoying to try to follow.”

I mean… I *want* to say that this is also a fair criticism, but also kind of… That first paragraph is fairly short, serving as a simple introduction to the segment, and the actual thesis itself is stated literally two sentences later. I suppose that the sentences *are* pretty big, so that might cause some issues with trying to follow along with my though, but still… it’s not like I waited multiple paragraphs to actually explain what I was talking about.

Dunno, maybe that’s just because I am extremely used to reading both books and essays with decently long-winded prose, so I don’t really have any issues retaining certain ideas from the opening parts until they are eventually revealed a few dozen/hundred words later, while someone who didn’t have as much exposure to the similar writing style could find themselves struggling to properly keep it all in their head. I’ll *try* to do better in the future, maybe, but I’m also not sure how much can I even change that aspect of how I write without just completely reinventing my comfortable and well-established approach to expressing myself through text.

Oh, you're near the sixth reset.
Suffice to say, he has certain... let's say, triggers. Nodoka is deliberately exploiting them. When you don't enable Haruka and her events, you just lie with Nodoka, as intended there. Otherwise, since Nodoka knows about Haruka's... proclivities, she drags both Sensei and her into more depravity, Haruka willing and Sensei... let's say, primed. You should already have a basic understanding of Sensei, this is just another look into it.
That said, if you're curious and will keep on with the game, here's is a sneak peek that may or may not be real. If you do want to quit, no problem, because this game really isn't for everyone.
So you are here, then.
Go on.
Watch me.
I don’t care if you do.
I don’t care if that curiosity reaches its boiling point because I know what it’s like on the opposite end.
And if there are more people like me in this world, maybe it’ll be harder for me to realize just how far I’ve fallen.
Maybe you’ll fall too. Maybe you already have. And maybe you want me to catch you.
I will. Just like she caught me. And I will ruin you. Just like she ruined me.
But it will be a lesson in love — one that you take to the grave and look back on both fondly and sickly when things don’t work out. Because, let’s face it — there’s no way they ever could.
The two of us have nothing in common apart from a desire to escape the endless torment that is feeling out of place even when you know you’re not.
Or, you know...maybe there’s something else we have in common too. Because you’re the one who’s choosing to watch right now. I’m not making you do anything.
I have learned nothing from these mistakes. And some of them have brought the happiest days of my life.
And while that doesn’t say much in a life of tragedy after tragedy, maybe it will say something for you.
Maybe one more mistake won’t cause my world to end — but yours did the moment you decided to keep your eyes open.
The floodgates have opened.
But if the water is too violent, I won’t worry.
I’ll just wait for it all to reset.
All said, Nodoka really is a bit of a plot device more than a character. She has her moments, but they are very few and sometimes overshadowed by her other actions.

Otherwise, since Nodoka knows about Haruka's... proclivities, she drags both Sensei and her into more depravity, Haruka willing and Sensei... let's say, primed. You should already have a basic understanding of Sensei, this is just another look into it.
That said, if you're curious and will keep on with the game, here's is a sneak peek that may or may not be real. If you do want to quit, no problem, because this game really isn't for everyone.
So you are here, then.
Go on.
Watch me.
I don’t care if you do.
I don’t care if that curiosity reaches its boiling point because I know what it’s like on the opposite end.
And if there are more people like me in this world, maybe it’ll be harder for me to realize just how far I’ve fallen.
Maybe you’ll fall too. Maybe you already have. And maybe you want me to catch you.
I will. Just like she caught me. And I will ruin you. Just like she ruined me.
But it will be a lesson in love — one that you take to the grave and look back on both fondly and sickly when things don’t work out. Because, let’s face it — there’s no way they ever could.
The two of us have nothing in common apart from a desire to escape the endless torment that is feeling out of place even when you know you’re not.
Or, you know...maybe there’s something else we have in common too. Because you’re the one who’s choosing to watch right now. I’m not making you do anything.
I have learned nothing from these mistakes. And some of them have brought the happiest days of my life.
And while that doesn’t say much in a life of tragedy after tragedy, maybe it will say something for you.
Maybe one more mistake won’t cause my world to end — but yours did the moment you decided to keep your eyes open.
The floodgates have opened.
But if the water is too violent, I won’t worry.
I’ll just wait for it all to reset.
All said, Nodoka really is a bit of a plot device more than a character. She has her moments, but they are very few and sometimes overshadowed by her other actions.

Cuz she's cool and a lot of her events advanced the actual plot.
