posts.content_html_raw:
This is part 2 of my series of theory posts on the Nagasawas. Part 1 is here.

This post won't answer the question I teased last time ("Why did Sensei dream that Nodoka is his sister?") because I have since realized that answer needs more setup than I can fit in a single post. So instead of a big theory, I want to establish an idea I will build on later: Nodoka and the Kyoko in the upside down house are linked to each other through their dreams.
During Nodoka's manic episodes, she sees things from another place. She experiences this as a sort of waking dream when she closes her eyes.
Specifically, she's seeing things from the upside down house.
These thoughts come from someone that Nodoka calls "a second me".
Almost every clue points to this being Kyoko. When Nodoka retells events from the upside down house, they're always from Kyoko's perspective.
"Beyond the Reach of God":


"Lavender":


This is a bit of a fun one: the "uninspired moniker" refers to her pen name, S. A. Nagahara. She's saying that Kyoko still remembers the screams from when "A" (Ai) found the dead body of "S" (Shiori).

"Partial to Jasmine":


"When the Well Runs Dry":
In addition, Nodoka shares certain traits with Kyoko that seem to go beyond just mother-daughter resemblance. In some ways Nodoka really is "a second Kyoko":
  • They look almost identical (Shiori's reaction in "F4972-B")
  • They are both obsessed with a "lavender girl" who they want to marry despite the other girl's lack of interest. Kyoko with Yuko and her lavender hair, Nodoka with Futaba and her lavender perfume.
  • They both have a love of books and a dislike of poetry. The way Nodoka talks about this, it's more than just a hobby they happen to share.
There is, however, one clue pointing to someone else as the "second me": Nodoka blamed her outbursts on her "evil twin" Shiori.
I can't think of any way this could actually be true, though. During her episodes, Nodoka rants from a perspective that clearly isn't Shiori's, and manic outbursts seem really out character for the Shiori we met. So I struggle to explain why Nodoka referred to Shiori in this way; If anyone else has an idea, I'd love to hear it.
Nodoka has waking visions because of her connection with Kyoko. It's rarer, but the connection goes the other way as well. The Kyoko in the house has dreams of Nodoka that feel as real as memories.

(Note: I can't be certain this is Kyoko speaking or that she's talking about Nodoka, but as I argued last time it fits with the other tweets where both of those things are true.)
More importantly, the two Nagasawas shared a dream, one in which they see a girl with with blue eyes. Kyoko tweeted about it and also wrote the same thing in her journal (which might suggest the AreYouHappyHere tweets are things written in Kyoko's journal, by her or the other girls). She implies that she's dreamed of the girl more than once.
Nodoka has also dreamed of her multiple times, and she explicitly wonders if she's dreaming about the same girl as Kyoko.

("long, tubular objects" = wires?)
Note also how she describes Kyoko's dreams as "the memories that precede my own", further suggesting that Kyoko is the "second me" whose memories Nodoka is seeing.

I think this dream is important enough that it's worth talking about why it's happening, even though the topic is a bit of a diversion.
The Nagasawas both dreamed about a blue-eyed girl. Nodoka recognized Himawari when they met on the roof, coming close to confirming that she was the girl from the dreams.
She may have started to say "You're the one she dreamed of". It's a little odd she says this instead of "You're the one I dreamed of", but maybe it means she thinks the dreams originally come from Kyoko, rather than the other way around.

In the last reset, we got a very good explanation for why Nodoka would dream about Himawari. This time Shiori was the one to reset Nodoka, and Nodoka remembered her in the form of a dream.

Nodoka has "memories" of Shiori from the upside down house - but to her, that's both another world and something that happened in the past.
This seems to be how her brain attempts to make sense of memories that weren't quite fully erased. This is just speculation, but I'm guessing they weren't fully erased because of her link with Kyoko. The custodian erases everything in Nodoka's own brain, but maybe rough impressions of some memories bleed over to Kyoko, and after the reset rough impressions of those rough impressions make their way back to Nodoka.

Prior to this latest reset, Himawari was the one who reset Nodoka along with the rest of the world. So Nodoka was having dreams of Himawari for the same reason she had a dream of Shiori this time: impressions of the reset managed to carry over. This fits the timing as well. Nodoka first talks about her dream of the blue-eyed girl late in Chapter 2 (without specifying when she had the dream). Then in her first appearance in Chapter 3, she says she had the dream again, linking it to the reset which just happened.

Which brings us to the big question: why did Kyoko also dream about a blue-eyed girl? The way I see it, there are two main possibilities:
  1. Kyoko dreamed about Himawari purely because Nodoka dreamed about Himawari and these dreams leaked through the link between them.
  2. Kyoko's dreams of Himawari are her own leftover remnants of being reset, i.e. Himawari was resetting the girls in the house in addition to the girls in Sensei's world.
(Technically it's also possible Kyoko was dreaming of a completely different blue-eyed girl and the whole thing is a coincidence, but I see no reason for Selebus to do that.)
#1 is what I've hinted at so far, and what I ultimately believe at the moment, but both options have some interesting implications worth discussing.

To begin with, there's a decent chance that the girls in the upside down house were in fact being reset. If you look at the timeline of the twitter, there are tweets where everything seems to be fine, followed by tweets where things are going wrong and at least one of the girls is dead, followed by tweets where things are back to fine and it's implied that everyone is alive. Either the house was reset in between these, or the tweets are completely jumbled up rather than in chronological order.

On the other hand, we can say with near certainty that the game's Himawari has no memory of the upside down house. Unless she was putting on one hell of an act, she's clueless about the connection between Shiori and the Nagasawas.
In addition, she said she's very new to her custodian job and doesn't seem to be any older than her physical age, while the events from the twitter seem to be from long before the start of the game. This doesn't rule out Himawari's involvement entirely; it's possible that some previous version of Himawari became a custodian and was involved with the house before being reset, leaving the current version completely in the dark.

But since we have essentially zero evidence for Himawari's historical involvement, the alternative seems more likely: Kyoko only dreams about her because of her involvement with Nodoka. But again, Himawari's involvement with Nodoka is a recent thing, while Kyoko's tweet about the dream should have happened long before the game. So it would seem that this requires that the Nagasawa link goes backward in time, as well: Kyoko in the past experienced things happening to Nodoka in the present. I don't particularly like the idea, so I'm still keeping an open mind about things.
Next time I'll finally address the topic of Sensei's sister, though after this post you might have already guessed where I'm going with that.

Kyoko dreamed about Himawari purely because Nodoka dreamed about Himawari and these dreams leaked through the link between them.
Kyoko's dreams of Himawari are her own leftover remnants of being reset, i.e. Himawari was resetting the girls in the house in addition to the girls in Sensei's world.
(Technically it's also possible Kyoko was dreaming of a completely different blue-eyed girl and the whole thing is a coincidence, but I see no reason for Selebus to do that.)
#1 is what I've hinted at so far, and what I ultimately believe at the moment, but both options have some interesting implications worth discussing.
To begin with, there's a decent chance that the girls in the upside down house were in fact being reset. If you look at the timeline of the twitter, there are tweets where everything seems to be fine, followed by tweets where things are going wrong and at least one of the girls is dead, followed by tweets where things are back to fine and it's implied that everyone is alive. Either the house was reset in between these, or the tweets are completely jumbled up rather than in chronological order.
On the other hand, we can say with near certainty that the game's Himawari has no memory of the upside down house. Unless she was putting on one hell of an act, she's clueless about the connection between Shiori and the Nagasawas.
Spoiler
In addition, she said she's very new to her custodian job and doesn't seem to be any older than her physical age, while the events from the twitter seem to be from long before the start of the game. This doesn't rule out Himawari's involvement entirely; it's possible that some previous version of Himawari became a custodian and was involved with the house before being reset, leaving the current version completely in the dark.
But since we have essentially zero evidence for Himawari's historical involvement, the alternative seems more likely: Kyoko only dreams about her because of her involvement with Nodoka. But again, Himawari's involvement with Nodoka is a recent thing, while Kyoko's tweet about the dream should have happened long before the game. So it would seem that this requires that the Nagasawa link goes backward in time, as well: Kyoko in the past experienced things happening to Nodoka in the present. I don't particularly like the idea, so I'm still keeping an open mind about things.
Next time I'll finally address the topic of Sensei's sister, though after this post you might have already guessed where I'm going with that.

I agree with you; The upside down house is almost certainly stuck in a Timeloop situation as well. From my own memories of the many times it's appeared in the game, something has always been wrong about it. Weird shit, and all that.

That matches with my own beliefs, which you mirror, that Nodoka has memories of the resets due to memory leakage from failed memory wipes. It may have some relation to Ami's situation, with her potentially being overwritten by the memories of "Ami-Psycho-Prime".

Fantastic write up! It's crazy to me how some of you guys have such amazing memories for the little details in this game.

I do, though, still think Nodoka is Akira's actual daughter. There are a lot of years still missing from his history, so him meeting, fucking, and impregnating Kyoko is certainly possible.

Someone else may remember better than I do, but I remember Nodoka having a very peculiar reaction when she learned his name was Akira, and it was shortly after that, that she started calling him "Father". Father, instead of the more kink adjacent "Daddy".

Does anyone know if Nodoka calls her mom "Mother?" I don't recall, someone else might.

She might call him that in the religious sense, though, since she seems to speak a lot in religious allegory.

Mysteries abound!

Finally:

We "know" that Akira's brother is the God of Wires, right? Or something along those lines? Correct me if I'm wrong here, but it's something like that. Definitely a god of some sort.

I have to wonder if, all the weird memory shit, is due to that familial relationship.

Ami - Been in the Timeloop longer than Maya? Potentially is actually Akira's daughter. Potentially is Nozomu's daughter. Alt universe Ami IS Akira's daughter(Implied), so makes sense. Could be a dying wish from Sekai.

Himiwari - IS Akira's daughter. Breaks free of the universe to become a janitor or whatever? Outside of timeloops.

Ayane - Impregnated by Akira, becomes aware of the timeloops.

Nodoka - Might be his daughter, aware of the timeloops, has weird memories and dreams.

Maya - Wish from Akira(Which is kinda like a daughter). Aware of the Timeloop(Prime).

I dunno, mostly just rambling, but I have to wonder if there is something to it. Yasu makes it clear that there is some sort of energy transfer when you fuck Akira, which might be related in some way.

The demo was from 2019, but seeing as some of those Characters have since appeared IN Lessons In Love, it's obviously all the same universe.

aramaug said:
This is part 2 of my series of theory posts on the Nagasawas. Part 1 is
here
.
This post won't answer the question I teased last time ("Why did Sensei dream that Nodoka is his sister?") because I have since realized that answer needs more setup than I can fit in a single post. So instead of a big theory, I want to establish an idea I will build on later:
Nodoka and the Kyoko in the upside down house are linked to each other through their dreams
.
Spoiler:
Nodoka's dreams
During Nodoka's manic episodes, she sees things from another place. She experiences this as a sort of waking dream when she closes her eyes.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945055
View attachment 5945059
Specifically, she's seeing things from the upside down house.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945062
View attachment 5945063
View attachment 5945064
These thoughts come from someone that Nodoka calls "a second me".
Spoiler
View attachment 5945072
Almost every clue points to this being Kyoko. When Nodoka retells events from the upside down house, they're always from Kyoko's perspective.
Spoiler
"Beyond the Reach of God":
View attachment 5946152
View attachment 5946153
"Lavender":
View attachment 5946224
View attachment 5945078
This is a bit of a fun one: the "uninspired moniker" refers to her pen name, S. A. Nagahara. She's saying that Kyoko still remembers the screams from when "A" (Ai) found the dead body of "S" (Shiori).
"Partial to Jasmine":
View attachment 5945089
"When the Well Runs Dry":
View attachment 5945100
In addition, Nodoka shares certain traits with Kyoko that seem to go beyond just mother-daughter resemblance. In some ways Nodoka really is "a second Kyoko":
They look almost identical (Shiori's reaction in "F4972-B")
They are both obsessed with a "lavender girl" who they want to marry despite the other girl's lack of interest. Kyoko with Yuko and her lavender hair, Nodoka with Futaba and her lavender perfume.
They both have a love of books and a dislike of poetry. The way Nodoka talks about this, it's more than just a hobby they happen to share.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945105
There is, however, one clue pointing to someone else as the "second me": Nodoka blamed her outbursts on her "evil twin" Shiori.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945108
I can't think of any way this could actually be true, though. During her episodes, Nodoka rants from a perspective that clearly isn't Shiori's, and manic outbursts seem really out character for the Shiori we met. So I struggle to explain why Nodoka referred to Shiori in this way; If anyone else has an idea, I'd love to hear it.
Spoiler:
Kyoko's dreams
Nodoka has waking visions because of her connection with Kyoko. It's rarer, but the connection goes the other way as well. The Kyoko in the house has dreams of Nodoka that feel as real as memories.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945112
(Note: I can't be certain this is Kyoko speaking or that she's talking about Nodoka, but as I argued last time it fits with the other tweets where both of those things are true.)
More importantly, the two Nagasawas shared a dream, one in which they see a girl with with blue eyes. Kyoko tweeted about it and also wrote the same thing in her journal (which might suggest the AreYouHappyHere tweets are things written in Kyoko's journal, by her or the other girls). She implies that she's dreamed of the girl more than once.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945113
View attachment 5945116
View attachment 5945120
View attachment 5945127
Nodoka has also dreamed of her multiple times, and she explicitly wonders if she's dreaming about the same girl as Kyoko.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945130
View attachment 5945135
("long, tubular objects" = wires?)
View attachment 5945138
View attachment 5945142
Note also how she describes Kyoko's dreams as "the memories that precede my own", further suggesting that Kyoko is the "second me" whose memories Nodoka is seeing.
I think this dream is important enough that it's worth talking about why it's happening, even though the topic is a bit of a diversion.
Spoiler:
Why is Kyoko dreaming about Himawari?
The Nagasawas both dreamed about a blue-eyed girl. Nodoka recognized Himawari when they met on the roof, coming close to confirming that she was the girl from the dreams.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945143
View attachment 5945146
She may have started to say "You're the one she dreamed of". It's a little odd she says this instead of "You're the one I dreamed of", but maybe it means she thinks the dreams originally come from Kyoko, rather than the other way around.
In the last reset, we got a very good explanation for why Nodoka would dream about Himawari. This time Shiori was the one to reset Nodoka, and Nodoka remembered her in the form of a dream.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945151
View attachment 5945152
Nodoka has "memories" of Shiori from the upside down house - but to her, that's both another world and something that happened in the past.
This seems to be how her brain attempts to make sense of memories that weren't quite fully erased. This is just speculation, but I'm guessing they weren't fully erased because of her link with Kyoko. The custodian erases everything in Nodoka's own brain, but maybe rough impressions of some memories bleed over to Kyoko, and after the reset rough impressions of those rough impressions make their way back to Nodoka.
Prior to this latest reset, Himawari was the one who reset Nodoka along with the rest of the world. So Nodoka was having dreams of Himawari for the same reason she had a dream of Shiori this time: impressions of the reset managed to carry over. This fits the timing as well. Nodoka first talks about her dream of the blue-eyed girl late in Chapter 2 (without specifying when she had the dream). Then in her first appearance in Chapter 3, she says she had the dream again, linking it to the reset which just happened.
Which brings us to the big question: why did Kyoko also dream about a blue-eyed girl? The way I see it, there are two main possibilities:
Kyoko dreamed about Himawari purely because Nodoka dreamed about Himawari and these dreams leaked through the link between them.
Kyoko's dreams of Himawari are her own leftover remnants of being reset, i.e. Himawari was resetting the girls in the house in addition to the girls in Sensei's world.
(Technically it's also possible Kyoko was dreaming of a completely different blue-eyed girl and the whole thing is a coincidence, but I see no reason for Selebus to do that.)
#1 is what I've hinted at so far, and what I ultimately believe at the moment, but both options have some interesting implications worth discussing.
To begin with, there's a decent chance that the girls in the upside down house were in fact being reset. If you look at the timeline of the twitter, there are tweets where everything seems to be fine, followed by tweets where things are going wrong and at least one of the girls is dead, followed by tweets where things are back to fine and it's implied that everyone is alive. Either the house was reset in between these, or the tweets are completely jumbled up rather than in chronological order.
On the other hand, we can say with near certainty that the game's Himawari has no memory of the upside down house. Unless she was putting on one hell of an act, she's clueless about the connection between Shiori and the Nagasawas.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945155
View attachment 5945156
In addition, she said she's very new to her custodian job and doesn't seem to be any older than her physical age, while the events from the twitter seem to be from long before the start of the game. This doesn't rule out Himawari's involvement entirely; it's possible that some previous version of Himawari became a custodian and was involved with the house before being reset, leaving the current version completely in the dark.
But since we have essentially zero evidence for Himawari's historical involvement, the alternative seems more likely: Kyoko only dreams about her because of her involvement with Nodoka. But again, Himawari's involvement with Nodoka is a recent thing, while Kyoko's tweet about the dream should have happened long before the game. So it would seem that this requires that the Nagasawa link goes backward in time, as well: Kyoko in the past experienced things happening to Nodoka in the present. I don't particularly like the idea, so I'm still keeping an open mind about things.
Next time I'll finally address the topic of Sensei's sister, though after this post you might have already guessed where I'm going with that.

On the other hand, we can say with near certainty that the game's Himawari has no memory of the upside down house. Unless she was putting on one hell of an act, she's clueless about the connection between Shiori and the Nagasawas.
Spoiler
View attachment 5945155
View attachment 5945156
In addition, she said she's very new to her custodian job and doesn't seem to be any older than her physical age, while the events from the twitter seem to be from long before the start of the game. This doesn't rule out Himawari's involvement entirely; it's possible that some previous version of Himawari became a custodian and was involved with the house before being reset, leaving the current version completely in the dark.
But since we have essentially zero evidence for Himawari's historical involvement, the alternative seems more likely: Kyoko only dreams about her because of her involvement with Nodoka. But again, Himawari's involvement with Nodoka is a recent thing, while Kyoko's tweet about the dream should have happened long before the game. So it would seem that this requires that the Nagasawa link goes backward in time, as well: Kyoko in the past experienced things happening to Nodoka in the present. I don't particularly like the idea, so I'm still keeping an open mind about things.

posts.content_html_raw:
Finished Chapter 2 today, took little over 50 hours. I feel like within first 15h the cast literally doubled. I lowkey expect Uta's thing to be even more fucked than Io for some reason. I swear that Kirin got like 2x or even 3x more screentime than some other girls in this chapter. Otoha feels like her entire purpose is to be drama enabler for Rin. Not sure about Nodoka yet. Touka feels like borderline secondary/comedy character so far, I hope they will do something with her other than being glued to Yasu, who shapes up to be walking plot device. Pink sisters got and probably will continue to get more presence and relevancy than most due to their connection with Sensei, but I like both a lot, that event with Noriko giving the box during Christmas was so good.

Regarding original girls, Rin's and Yumi's arcs still carry the rest and I see that going for a while, but Miku got the most development (and best render in almost 100 hours in) in this chapter by far. That Makoto's bluejay thing from the end of Chapter 1 wasn't elaborated on much, but I'm sure it will come back. I have no idea what to say about Futaba, I guess that she... started to work out? Same with Sana, hasn't really changed much yet, still shy, jealous cockblocker in making, but her brother got ganked apparently, best mom still ofc. Wild guess, but I will throw loose prediction that Chika will fuck up big in the future, Sensei will tell her to chill and/or gtfo and she will go yandere. Dunno what to say about Ami, Maya and now Ayane I guess, since their arcs are probably going to be completely tied to the "main" story.

I've somehow managed to do all puzzles alone up to and including 4th reset, but I'm officially done, expecting to note down every number which shows up on the screen and in TTS loops is a kind of autism that I actually find to be quite endearing, but having to note down solitare trivia, bathtub gallons and click on rice was pure retardation. And those snarky 4th wall comments about players and puzzles are just eyeroll worthy.

Now, when it comes to the main story so far, I obviously want to see where it will go, but honestly, I think that at this point I'm more interested in individual character's stories and interactions. Like, if you put all this supernatural stuff, convenient world and everyone falling for the dick aside, I get that Sensei is what he is and acts like he acts due to some massive trauma, with "Good Boy" Secret Event implying that he was molested by his teacher, who was Ami's mom by the way what the fuck, also, really curious why this event requires Sara's event to be seen. Abuse victims continuing the circle of abuse etc.
The thing I really, really wouldn't like to see, is this turning to be "yeah I'm bad, really bad, I do bad things which I know are bad and it makes me bad, but I'm beyond fixing, this is who I am, you know who are you dealing with" going till the end without any real consequence or challenge. But I'm not even halfway through released material, which isn't even close to the finish of the game overall from what I know, so maybe it won't go in that direction. Also, really bad vibes from flashbacks with loli Maya on top of him and that weird choice with Chinami bathing, so preying on high school students might not be the rock bottom here.
